definition_zh: 河口湾（河流入海口淡水与海水混合的宽阔水域）；潮汐河口；河口生态系统
definition_en: the wide lower part of a river where fresh water meets the sea and is mixed by the tides
core_image: 浑黄的河水在喇叭形的入海口被咸蓝的海水顶回来，潮水一涨一落，泥滩时而淹没时而露出
scene: 退潮后，喇叭形的入海口露出大片泥滩，海鸥沿着浅水道觅食。 At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
sceneCN: 这里 estuary 指「河流入海处淡水与海水交汇的宽阔水域」（第 1 个义项：河口湾）；句意：退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。图中可辨识物件：泥滩上的浅水道、觅食的海鸥、河与海交界处的水色、搁浅的小船。

pos.zh: 河口湾；河口（河流入海处淡水与海水交汇、受潮汐影响的水域）

forms.label: 形容词（河口湾的，较少用）

derivatives.zh: 河口湾的；生活在河口湾的
河口湾的（较少用的同义变体）
河口英语（泰晤士河口一带的英语口音）
河口湾口门（河流与海相接的出口）
河口环境（淡咸水交汇的生境）

senses.title: The wide mouth where river meets sea
senses.titleCN: 河口湾：河流入海处的宽阔水域
senses.definition: the wide lower reach of a river where its fresh water meets and mixes with sea water
senses.definitionCN: 河流下游宽阔的河段，淡水在此与海水相遇并混合
senses.example: At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。
senses.why: the word names the drowned lower valley itself, a body of water wider than the river because the sea has invaded it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指被海水侵入的下游河谷本身；因为海水的进入，它比河道更宽。

senses.title: A tidal reach governed by the tide
senses.definition: the part of a river near its mouth in which the water level and the direction of flow reverse with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 河流近口门、水位与流向随潮汐往复变化的那一段
senses.example: Salt water pushes upstream in the estuary with every flood tide.
senses.exampleCN: 每次涨潮，咸水都沿河口段向上游推进。
senses.why: the tidal sense narrows the first: the same water body is defined by the twice-daily reversal of its current.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐义收窄了第一个义项：同一片水域，以水流一日两次反向为界定特征。

senses.title: A brackish ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 河口生态系统（淡咸水交汇的生境）
senses.definition: the community of plants and animals adapted to water whose salinity changes with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 适应盐度随潮汐变化的河口水的动植物群落
senses.example: Juvenile salmon feed in the estuary before they enter the open sea.
senses.exampleCN: 幼鲑在进入外海之前先在河口育肥。
senses.why: from the place the word passes to what lives in it, a standard shift from a habitat to its community.
senses.whyCN: 由地点转向其中的生物，这是从生境到生物群落的常见转喻。

senses.title: Silt laid down at the river mouth
senses.titleCN: 河口沉积（河流泥沙在口门堆积）
senses.definition: sand and mud carried down by the river and deposited where the current slows at the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 河流带下的砂与泥在口门流速减缓处堆积而成的沉积物
senses.example: Cores from the estuary record two centuries of upstream soil erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 河口沉积柱芯记录了两个世纪的上游水土流失。
senses.why: the estuary is a sediment trap, so its name transfers to the material that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 河口是泥沙的捕集器，因此其名称也转指填在其中的物质。

senses.title: Fishing and farming in estuarine water
senses.definition: the use of nutrient-rich estuarine water for catching fish or cultivating shellfish
senses.definitionCN: 利用营养丰富的河口水域捕鱼或养殖贝类
senses.example: Oyster farms in the estuary depend on clean water and steady tides.
senses.exampleCN: 河口湾的牡蛎养殖场依赖洁净的水与稳定的潮汐。
senses.why: human activity is named by its setting, as with any fishery; the estuary supplies the nutrients that make the catch possible.
senses.whyCN: 人类活动以所在地命名，正如各类渔场；河口提供养分，才使捕捞成为可能。

senses.title: Pollution where the river meets the sea
senses.definition: the accumulation of pollutants in estuarine water, where river discharge and sea water mix and currents are slow
senses.definitionCN: 污染物在河口水中的累积，该处河水与海水混合、流速缓慢
senses.example: Nitrogen from farms collects in the estuary and feeds summer algal blooms.
senses.exampleCN: 农田带来的氮在河口积聚，助长夏季藻华。
senses.why: because the estuary is the collecting basin of a whole catchment, its name becomes shorthand for the water-quality problem there.
senses.whyCN: 河口是整个流域的汇集盆，因此其名称成为当地水质问题的代称。

senses.title: A dredged channel for shipping
senses.definition: the navigable channel maintained through an estuary for ships moving between the river and the sea
senses.definitionCN: 为船舶进出河流与海洋而在河口维护的通航水道
senses.example: Dredging keeps the estuary open to ships drawing twelve metres.
senses.exampleCN: 疏浚使河口航道可供吃水十二米的船舶通行。
senses.why: the mouth is the gate of a river port, so the word also names the passage that has to be kept open.
senses.whyCN: 口门是河港的门户，因此这个词也指必须维持畅通的那条通道。

senses.title: A meeting ground of unlike things
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不同事物的交汇地带
senses.definition: a place or situation in which two different systems meet and influence each other
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同体系相遇并相互影响的地方或处境
senses.example: The festival became an estuary of rural and urban tastes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆成了乡村与城市趣味的交汇地带。
senses.why: the physical mixing of fresh and salt water is generalized into any boundary zone where unlike things blend.
senses.whyCN: 淡水与咸水的物理混合被一般化为任何不同事物交融的边界地带。

intro.en: Estuary comes from Latin aestuarium 'a tract flooded by the tide', from aestus 'tide, surge, heat'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. The deeper origin of aestus is uncertain, and the link sometimes proposed with aestas 'summer' is a hypothesis.
intro.cn: estuary 来自拉丁 aestuarium「受潮水淹没的滩地」，后者出自 aestus「潮汐、涌动、热」。英语于 16 世纪借入。aestus 的更深来源不确定，有人提出它与 aestas「夏天」有关，但那只是假说。

items.en: Aestus meant 'tide, surge' and also 'boiling, seething heat'. Roman writers used it for both the movement of the sea and the fever of the body.
items.cn: aestus 意为「潮汐、涌动」，也指「沸腾、灼热」。罗马作家用它既指海水的运动，也指身体的发热。

items.en: Aestuarium was the low ground or channel that the tide fills and empties; the suffix -arium marks a place associated with the action of aestus.
items.cn: aestuarium 指潮水灌入又退出的低地或水道；后缀 -arium 表示与 aestus 这一动作相关的地点。

items.en: English geographers borrowed aestuarium in the 1530s for the widened mouth of a tidal river, and the spelling settled as estuary.
items.cn: 16 世纪 30 年代，英国地理学者借入 aestuarium，用来指受潮汐影响的宽河口；拼写后来固定为 estuary。

items.en: The early English sense kept the tidal idea, so an estuary was a river mouth shaped by the rise and fall of the sea rather than merely the end of a river.
items.cn: 早期英语义保留了潮汐意味，因此河口湾指受海水涨落塑造的河口，而不只是河流的终点。

items.en: The adjective estuarine was formed in the nineteenth century on the model of Latin -inus, and estuarial followed as a rarer variant; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 estuarine 于 19 世纪仿拉丁 -inus 构成，estuarial 作为更少用的变体随后出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of aestus): the connection with aestas 'summer' and with Greek aithein 'to burn' are competing hypotheses, and any Indo-European form offered for aestus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（aestus 的更深词源）：与 aestas「夏天」以及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系是并行的假说，凡为 aestus 拟出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates estuary from look-alikes, including one word that shares its Latin root and several that do not; group two contrasts the tidal river mouth with neighbouring water features.
note.cn: 第一组把 estuary 与形近词分开，其中一词共享拉丁词根，其余并无关系；第二组把潮汐河口与相邻的水域概念作对比。

entries.definition: From Latin aestivus 'of summer', built on the same aest- base as aestus; it means 'summery' and does not name a river mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aestivus「夏天的」，与 aestus 共用 aest- 词干；意为「夏季的」，并不指河口。

entries.definition: The practice of lending money at interest, from Latin usura 'use'; the -ury ending makes it sound like estuary, but the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 指放贷取息的行业，来自拉丁 usura「使用」；-ury 词尾使它听起来像 estuary，但词根不同。

entries.definition: To alienate someone, from Latin extraneare 'treat as a stranger'; only the opening letters resemble estuary.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某人疏远，来自拉丁 extraneare「当作陌生人对待」；只有开头几个字母与 estuary 相似。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty, from Greek aisthanesthai 'to perceive'; the shared opening sound is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指与美有关的，来自希腊 aisthanesthai「感知」；开头的读音相近只是巧合。

entries.definition: A river mouth where the current slows and splits around deposited sediment; an estuary is instead a drowned valley dominated by tides.
entries.definitionCN: 河流因流速减缓、泥沙堆积而分汊的口门；河口湾则是被海水淹没、以潮汐为主导的河谷。

entries.definition: A Scottish word for a narrow sea inlet or river estuary; it overlaps with estuary but is regional.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语中指狭窄的海湾或河口；与 estuary 语义重叠，但属地域用词。

entries.definition: A narrow opening by which the sea enters the land; it need not receive a river, which an estuary always does.
entries.definitionCN: 海水伸入陆地的狭窄通道；它不一定有河流注入，而河口湾一定有。

entries.definition: The point where a river enters a larger body of water; it is neutral and does not imply tidal mixing or width.
entries.definitionCN: 河流进入更大水域的那一点；语气中立，不含潮汐混合或宽阔水域之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aestus 'tide' plus -arium 'place': the place that the tide fills and empties.
normal.cn: aestus「潮汐」加 -arium「地点」：潮水灌入又退出的那个地方。

normal.en: The family is estuary, estuarine and estuarial; the adjective is far more common in ecology than the noun is in speech.
normal.cn: 同族词是 estuary、estuarine 与 estuarial；形容词在生态学中的使用远多于名词在日常口语中的使用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the ecology: estuary ecosystem, estuary sediment, estuary pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生态义：河口生态系统、河口沉积物、河口污染。

normal.en: Geography pairs it with delta: a delta builds outward, while an estuary is a valley drowned inward by the sea.
normal.cn: 地理学把它与三角洲对举：三角洲向外堆出，河口湾则是被海水向内淹没的河谷。

normal.en: British references such as the Thames estuary and the Severn estuary name the tidal type most clearly.
normal.cn: 泰晤士河口与塞文河口这类英国实例最能说明潮汐河口这一类型。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway where two crowds push in opposite directions and neither can move freely.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口，两股人潮相向而行，谁也走不痛快。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of tea into which cold milk is poured: the boundary is where the colours first mix.
abstract.cn: 想象往一杯热茶里倒入冷牛奶：交界处正是两种颜色最先混开的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a market where two languages trade words across the same counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，两种语言在同一个柜台前交换词语。

examples.en: The estuary supports a nursery for young fish before they reach the open sea.
examples.cn: 这片河口湾为幼鱼提供育肥场所，之后它们才进入外海。

examples.en: Sediment cores from the estuary show how fast the surrounding hills eroded.
examples.cn: 取自河口的沉积柱芯显示周边山地侵蚀得有多快。

examples.en: Ships wait for high water before they enter the shallow estuary.
examples.cn: 船舶等高潮时才驶入这片浅水河口湾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estuary」读似「爱水求瑞」——河水一路爱水，到海口求个汇合之处，便是河口湾

root: 拉丁 aestuarium「高潮淹没的滩地」< aestus「潮汐、沸腾、热」；英语 16 世纪借入。aestus 更深来源不确定，与 aestas「夏天」及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系均属假说，非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one physical event: a river valley drowned by the sea, where fresh and salt water are stirred twice a day. From that place come the tidal reach, the brackish community, its sediment, its fisheries, its pollution, its shipping channel, and finally any zone where two worlds mix.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个自然事件展开：河谷被海水淹没，淡水与咸水一日两次被搅动。由此依次生出潮汐河段、淡咸水生物群落、河口沉积、渔业、污染、航道，最后泛指任何两个世界交融的地带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river mouth flooded by the tide, where fresh and salt water are stirred together.
core.cn: 核心意象：被潮水灌入的河口，淡水与咸水在此搅在一起。

branches.en: DROWNED MOUTH: the widened lower valley and its twice-daily reversal of flow.
branches.cn: 被淹的口门：加宽的下游河谷，以及一日两次反向的水流。

branches.en: BRACKISH COMMUNITY: the living community that tolerates shifting salinity.
branches.cn: 淡咸水群落：能耐受盐度变化的生物群落。

branches.en: SILT TRAP: the mouth as a basin where river sediment settles.
branches.cn: 泥沙捕集：口门作为河流沉积物沉降的盆地。

branches.en: WORKING WATER: fishing, pollution and navigation all concentrate at the same mouth.
branches.cn: 作业水域：渔业、污染与航运都集中在这同一个口门。

branches.en: MEETING GROUND: the physical mix becomes an image for any boundary between two systems.
branches.cn: 交汇地带：物理混合成为任何两个体系边界的意象。

intro.en: Estuary is a Latin loan whose parts can still be read: the root aestus 'tide' plus the place suffix -arium. English then added -ine and -al for the adjectives and joined the noun to native nouns in compounds.
intro.cn: estuary 是拉丁借词，其构词成分仍可读出：词根 aestus「潮汐」加地点后缀 -arium。英语随后加 -ine 与 -al 构成形容词，并与本族名词组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestus gives aestuarium and the verb aestuare 'to surge, boil'. Latin aestas 'summer' is a possible relative, but the link is debated rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aestus 衍生 aestuarium 与动词 aestuare「涌动、沸腾」。拉丁 aestas「夏天」可能是其亲属，但这一联系仍有争议，尚未确立。

items.example: Aestus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestus 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: a place associated with an action
items.example: The suffix turns an action into a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个动作变成一处地点。

items.example: The estuary opens into a cold sea.
items.exampleCN: 这片河口湾通向一片寒冷的海。

items.example: Estuarine mud supports dense worm populations.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾的淤泥养育了密集的沙蚕种群。

items.meaning: of an estuary, a rarer variant
items.example: Estuarial waters warm slowly in spring.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾水域在春季升温缓慢。

items.meaning: the outer opening of a tidal river
items.example: Fishing boats crossed the estuary mouth at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔船在黎明时越过河口湾口门。

items.meaning: a brackish habitat within an estuary
items.meaningCN: 河口湾内的淡咸水生境
items.example: The estuarine habitat shifts with every tide.
items.exampleCN: 河口的生境随每次潮汐而改变。

items.meaning: an estuary dominated by tidal flow
items.meaningCN: 以潮汐水流为主导的河口
items.example: A tidal estuary reverses its current twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 潮汐河口的水流一日两次反向。

items.meaning: a variety of English associated with the Thames estuary
items.meaningCN: 与泰晤士河口相关的英语口音
items.example: Estuary English spread far beyond its home region.
items.exampleCN: 河口英语传播到了其发源地区之外很远的地方。

definition_zh: 反动的；反对变革的；反动分子
definition_en: opposing political or social change, often wanting to return to an earlier order
core_image: 一扇旧门被几个人合力顶住，门后的人还在喊「退回去」
scene: 镇上的老议员一听要拆旧钟楼，立刻站出来反对任何改动。 The reactionary alderman opposed every plan to pull down the old clock tower.
sceneCN: 这里 reactionary 指反动的、反对变革的（第 1 个义项：反对改革）；句意为镇上的老议员一听要拆旧钟楼，立刻站出来反对任何改动。

derivatives.zh: 反应；反动
反动主义

senses.title: Opposed to change
senses.titleCN: 反动的；反对变革的（形容词）
senses.definition: opposing political or social change and wishing to restore an earlier order
senses.definitionCN: 反对政治或社会变革，希望恢复旧秩序的
senses.example: The reactionary policy rolled back the housing rules passed a year earlier.
senses.exampleCN: 这项反动政策撤销了一年以前通过的住房规定。
senses.why: The adjective is the label used in debate: it accuses a measure of moving backwards.
senses.whyCN: 形容词形态是辩论里用的标签：它指控一项措施在往后退。

senses.title: A person of that view
senses.definition: a person who works to undo reforms and bring back the old order
senses.definitionCN: 致力于撤销改革、恢复旧秩序的人
senses.example: The old reactionary called every new machine a waste of money.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老反动派把每一台新机器都称作浪费钱。
senses.why: The noun turns the accusation into an identity, which is why it is often a fighting word.
senses.whyCN: 名词形态把指控变成一种身份，所以它常常是骂战里的词。

intro.en: Reactionary comes from reaction, from Latin re- 'back' plus agere 'to do', and was first applied to politics after the French Revolution.
intro.cn: reactionary 来自 reaction，源于拉丁语 re-（向后）加 agere（做），法国大革命之后才用于政治。

items.en: Agere meant to do or drive.
items.cn: agere 意为做、驱动。

items.en: Re-action was a doing back, a return movement.
items.cn: re-action 是「做回去」，一种回退的运动。

items.en: French politics named those who wished to undo the revolution.
items.cn: 法国政治把想撤销革命的人命名出来。

items.en: English carried the label into debates on reform.
items.cn: 英语把这个标签带入改革的辩论。

items.en: The word now marks resistance to change in many fields.
items.cn: 今天这个词标记许多领域里对变革的抵抗。

note.en: The look-alike group is the react- family; the near-meaning group separates conservative, diehard, traditionalist and ultraconservative.
note.cn: 形近组是 react 词族；近义组把「保守的」「死硬的」「传统主义者」「极端保守的」分开。

entries.definition: a response to an event.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件作出的回应。

entries.definition: responding rather than initiating.
entries.definitionCN: 回应而非主动的。

entries.definition: a vessel or plant where reactions occur.
entries.definitionCN: 发生反应的容器或装置。

entries.definition: the creed of reversing reform.
entries.definitionCN: 主张倒转改革的信条。

entries.definition: cautious about change.
entries.definitionCN: 对变革持谨慎态度的。

entries.definition: refusing to give up an old position.
entries.definitionCN: 拒不放弃旧立场的。

entries.definition: one who defends inherited practice.
entries.definitionCN: 捍卫沿袭做法的人。

entries.definition: extremely resistant to change.
entries.definitionCN: 极端抗拒变革的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of people holding an old door shut against a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一群人合力顶住旧门，不让外面的人进来」的画面。

normal.en: Reactionary is reaction plus ary: a person who does back.
normal.cn: reactionary 是 reaction 加 ary：一个「做回去」的人。

normal.en: Picture hands pressed on a door that should have been replaced.
normal.cn: 想象一双手按在一扇早该换掉的门上。

normal.en: Say ree-AK-shun-air-ee; the stress sits on AK.
normal.cn: 读 ree-AK-shun-air-ee，重音在 AK。

normal.en: The word is not neutral: it always accuses.
normal.cn: 这个词不中性：它总是在指控。

normal.en: Ask what is being restored, and for whom.
normal.cn: 问一句：要恢复的是什么，为谁恢复？

abstract.en: Reactionary measures time backwards: it treats an earlier order as the future.
abstract.cn: reactionary 把时间倒着量：它把旧秩序当作未来。

abstract.en: The label is a weapon in debate before it is a description of belief.
abstract.cn: 这个标签在成为信念的描述之前，先是一场辩论里的武器。

abstract.en: Every reactionary claim borrows the language of stability to justify reversal.
abstract.cn: 每一种反动主张都借稳定之名，为倒转辩护。

examples.en: Reactionary forces in the senate blocked the vote for months.
examples.cn: 参议院里的反动势力把表决拖了几个月。

examples.en: The reactionary policy rolled back the housing rules passed a year earlier.
examples.cn: 这项反动政策撤销了一年以前通过的住房规定。

examples.en: A conservative slows a reform; a reactionary tries to repeal it.
examples.cn: 保守派让改革变慢，反动派则想废除改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）+ action（行动）+ ary（人）→ 往回想把时间扳回去的人。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ agere（做）→ reaction（反动）+ -ary

sensesIntro.en: Reactionary has two senses, one for the policy and one for the person who holds it.
sensesIntro.cn: reactionary 有两层：一层说政策，一层说主张这种政策的人。

core.en: HANDS HOLDING AN OLD DOOR SHUT
core.cn: 双手按住一扇旧门

branches.en: A measure that undoes a reform.
branches.cn: 撤销改革的措施。

branches.en: A person whose identity is resistance.
branches.cn: 以抵抗为身份的人。

branches.en: The label as a weapon in debate.
branches.cn: 作为辩论武器的标签。

branches.en: Restoring an earlier order by force.
branches.cn: 以武力恢复旧秩序。

branches.en: The word accuses before it describes.
branches.cn: 这个词先指控，再描述。

intro.en: The react- family all turns on doing back: react, reaction, reactionary and reactionism keep one idea of return.
intro.cn: react 词族都围绕「做回去」：react、reaction、reactionary、reactionism 保留同一个回退的念头。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere gives act and action; with re- the compound means to drive back, which politics later turned into a label.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere 给出 act 与 action；加上 re- 表示「往回驱动」，政治后来把它变成一个标签。

definition_zh: 软骨；软骨组织；（食用肉中的）脆骨
definition_en: a firm but flexible connective tissue that is softer than bone and supports, cushions or shapes parts of the body
core_image: 一块半透明的弹性垫片，夹在两根硬骨之间，受力时压扁，松手后又弹回原状
scene: 解剖课上，老师把膝关节模型掰开，露出两片骨头之间的浅色垫层： The cartilage between the bones has worn thin.
sceneCN: 这里指「关节软骨」（第 2 个义项：覆盖骨端、减少摩擦的软骨层）；句意为两块骨头之间的软骨已经磨薄。图中可辨识物件：膝关节模型、两片骨端、浅色垫层、磨损标记。

senses.title: Flexible supporting tissue
senses.titleCN: 软骨组织：比骨软而有弹性的支持组织
senses.definition: a firm but flexible connective tissue that is softer than bone and holds shape without being rigid
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚实而有弹性、比骨软、能维持形状却不僵硬的结缔组织
senses.example: Cartilage gives the nose its shape without making it rigid.
senses.exampleCN: 软骨让鼻子成形，却不使它僵硬。
senses.why: Cartilage keeps its shape with a rubbery matrix instead of mineral deposits, so it bends before it breaks.
senses.whyCN: 软骨靠橡胶状的基质而非矿物沉积维持形状，因此先弯后断。

senses.title: Joint surface cushion
senses.titleCN: 关节软骨：覆盖骨端、减少摩擦
senses.definition: the smooth layer of cartilage covering the ends of bones where they meet in a joint
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在骨端接触处、使关节面光滑的软骨层
senses.example: Running on hard pavement for years wears away the cartilage in the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 多年在硬路面上跑步会磨掉膝关节的软骨。
senses.why: Two hard surfaces grinding together would soon fail, so a soft pad between them takes the friction and spreads the load.
senses.whyCN: 两块硬面直接研磨很快就会损坏，因此中间需要一层软垫承担摩擦、分散压力。

senses.title: Airway support
senses.titleCN: 呼吸道软骨：撑开管腔的环状支架
senses.definition: rings of cartilage that keep the trachea and larger airways open
senses.definitionCN: 使气管与较大气道保持张开的软骨环
senses.example: The rings of cartilage keep the trachea from collapsing when you breathe in.
senses.exampleCN: 软骨环让气管在吸气时不致塌陷。
senses.why: Soft tissue alone would close under pressure, so stiff but bendable cartilage acts as a permanent frame.
senses.whyCN: 只有软组织会在压力下闭合，因此需要坚硬又能弯曲的软骨充当常设支架。

senses.title: Elastic cartilage of ear and nose
senses.definition: cartilage rich in elastic fibres, found in the outer ear and the tip of the nose
senses.definitionCN: 富含弹性纤维、存在于外耳与鼻尖的软骨
senses.example: The cartilage in the ear bends easily and springs back into shape.
senses.exampleCN: 耳朵里的软骨容易弯折，又会弹回原形。
senses.why: Elastic fibres let the tissue return to its original form, which is why an ear can be folded and released.
senses.whyCN: 弹性纤维使组织能恢复原形，所以耳朵被折一下再松手还会回去。

senses.title: Cartilaginous skeleton
senses.titleCN: 软骨骨架：以软骨代替骨的支撑系统
senses.definition: a skeleton made mainly of cartilage rather than bone, as in sharks and rays
senses.definitionCN: 主要由软骨而非硬骨构成、见于鲨鱼与鳐鱼的骨架
senses.example: Sharks have a skeleton made mostly of cartilage rather than bone.
senses.exampleCN: 鲨鱼的骨架主要由软骨构成，而不是硬骨。
senses.why: The same flexible material that cushions a joint can also serve as the whole frame of an animal that needs to be light and mobile.
senses.whyCN: 用于缓冲关节的柔韧材料，也能整体充当骨架，适合需要轻便灵活的动物。

senses.title: Costal cartilage
senses.titleCN: 肋软骨：把肋骨连到胸骨
senses.definition: the bars of cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum and allow the chest to move
senses.definitionCN: 把肋骨连接到胸骨、使胸廓能够活动的软骨条
senses.example: Costal cartilage joins each rib to the sternum and flexes with every breath.
senses.exampleCN: 肋软骨把每根肋骨连到胸骨，并随呼吸弯动。
senses.why: A rigid joint would lock the ribcage, so cartilage supplies connection with just enough give for breathing.
senses.whyCN: 完全刚性的连接会锁住胸廓，因此用软骨连接，既连住又留有呼吸所需的余量。

senses.title: Avascular tissue that heals slowly
senses.titleCN: 无血管、修复缓慢的组织特性
senses.definition: cartilage contains no blood vessels, so damage to it repairs very slowly or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 软骨内部没有血管，因此受损后修复极慢，甚至不修复
senses.example: Because cartilage has no blood vessels, a torn joint surface heals very slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 由于软骨没有血管，撕裂的关节面修复得非常慢。
senses.why: Repair needs a blood supply to bring cells and material, and cartilage has none, which is why the cushion often stays worn.
senses.whyCN: 修复需要血液带来细胞与材料，而软骨没有血管，所以那层垫子常常一直磨损着。

senses.title: Gristle in food
senses.definition: the tough cartilage left in meat, hard to chew and usually trimmed away
senses.definitionCN: 留在肉里、难嚼、通常被剔除的坚韧软骨
senses.example: He cut away the cartilage before serving the chicken.
senses.exampleCN: 上鸡肉之前，他把脆骨剔掉了。
senses.why: This is the same tissue seen from the kitchen rather than the clinic: what supports a joint in the animal is simply tough gristle on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一组织在厨房而非诊室里的样子：支撑动物关节的东西，到了盘子里就是难嚼的脆骨。

intro.en: Cartilage comes through French from Latin cartilago, the anatomical word for gristle. The Latin noun is well attested, but its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cartilage 经法语来自拉丁语 cartilago，即「软骨、脆骨」的解剖用词。这个拉丁名词本身有充分书证，但其更深来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin cartilago (genitive cartilaginis) meant gristle or cartilage and was already used by Roman medical writers for the flexible parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cartilago（属格 cartilaginis）意为「软骨、脆骨」，罗马医学作者已用它指身体中柔韧的部分。

items.en: Source uncertain: the make-up of cartilago inside Latin cannot be demonstrated. A link to cratis wickerwork has been suggested because both describe a flexible lattice, and a link to caro flesh has also been proposed; neither is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：cartilago 在拉丁语内部如何构成无法证明。有人因「柔韧的网格」这一相似性提出它与 cratis「柳条编织物」有关，也有人提出与 caro「肉」有关，两种说法都未获证实。

items.en: Old French cartilage carried the word north, keeping the Latin medical sense rather than a everyday sense.
items.cn: 古法语 cartilage 把这个词向北传，保留的是拉丁医学义，而非日常义。

items.en: English records cartilage in the late fourteenth or early fifteenth century, in anatomical and medical writing.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末或 15 世纪初的解剖与医学文献中记录了 cartilage。

items.en: Anatomical Latin kept cartilago as the standard term and built the adjective cartilagineus, the source of English cartilaginous.
items.cn: 解剖学拉丁语以 cartilago 为标准术语，并构成形容词 cartilagineus，即英语 cartilaginous 的来源。

items.en: Nineteenth-century histology divided cartilage into hyaline, elastic and fibrous types. The exact first use of each subtype name is uncertain.
items.cn: 19 世纪组织学把软骨分为透明软骨、弹性软骨与纤维软骨三类，各亚型名称的最早使用年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to cartilage; the second holds tissues and everyday words with a related meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 cartilage 形近或音近的词；第二组是意思相关的组织名称与日常用词。

entries.definition: A case holding ammunition, or a container for ink. It ends in -ridge and shares no root with cartilage.
entries.definitionCN: 弹药筒，或墨盒。结尾是 -ridge，与 cartilage 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: The adjective of cartilage, meaning made of or relating to cartilage; it is not a separate noun.
entries.definitionCN: cartilage 的形容词，意为「软骨的、由软骨构成的」，并不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: The Greek combining form for cartilage, from chondros, used in chondrocyte and chondroitin; it is a different root from Latin cartilage.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语中表示软骨的构词成分，来自 chondros，用于 chondrocyte、chondroitin；它与拉丁语 cartilage 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: The Latin noun behind the English word, still used in anatomical Latin but not as an English everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 英语词背后的拉丁名词，仍用于解剖学拉丁语，但不是英语日常词。

entries.definition: Hard tissue strengthened by calcium minerals; cartilage is softer and has no mineralized matrix.
entries.definitionCN: 由钙质矿物强化的硬组织；软骨更软，基质没有矿化。

entries.definition: A tough band that ties bone to bone; cartilage is a supporting surface, not a connecting strap.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住的坚韧带状结构；软骨是承压表面，不是连接带。

entries.definition: A cord that attaches muscle to bone; it transmits pull rather than cushioning load.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的索状结构；它传递拉力，而不是缓冲压力。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for tough cartilage found in meat; it names the same tissue outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用语中指肉里的坚韧软骨；在非技术语境里指同一种组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin and Greek roots, real anatomical terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁与希腊词根、真实的解剖术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin cartilago is the direct source; English keeps almost the whole Latin stem, so the spelling can be rebuilt from the Latin noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cartilago 是直接来源；英语几乎保留了整个拉丁词干，因此拼写可由这个拉丁名词还原。

normal.en: Greek chondros gives the modern combining form chondro-, seen in chondrocyte and chondroitin.
normal.cn: 希腊语 chondros 提供现代构词成分 chondro-，见于 chondrocyte 与 chondroitin。

normal.en: Articular cartilage sits at the joint; costal cartilage sits at the ribs; both are named by the place they serve.
normal.cn: articular cartilage 位于关节，costal cartilage 位于肋骨，两者都按所服务的位置命名。

normal.en: Cartilage is avascular, so injuries heal slowly; this one fact explains most clinical talk about it.
normal.cn: 软骨无血管，因此损伤修复慢；这一事实解释了大多数关于它的临床讨论。

normal.en: Sharks are famous for a cartilaginous skeleton, which is why cartilage appears in zoology as well as medicine.
normal.cn: 鲨鱼以软骨骨架著称，所以 cartilage 不仅出现在医学里，也出现在动物学里。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber washer between two hard plates: it takes the grinding so the plates do not.
abstract.cn: 想象两片硬板之间垫着一个橡胶垫圈：由它承受研磨，硬板才得以保全。

abstract.en: Picture a bent ear that springs back the moment your fingers let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被折弯的耳朵，手指一松就弹回原状。

abstract.en: Picture a soft frame that slowly hardens into bone as a child grows, leaving the joints behind as permanent pads.
abstract.cn: 想象一副柔软的支架随孩子长大逐渐硬化成骨，只在关节处留下永久的软垫。

examples.en: The surgeon removed a loose piece of cartilage from the ankle joint.
examples.cn: 外科医生从踝关节取出了一块游离的软骨。

examples.en: A diet rich in collagen supports the cartilage that cushions the knees.
examples.cn: 富含胶原蛋白的饮食有助于支撑膝关节的软骨。

examples.en: Engineers are testing a gel that may one day regrow damaged cartilage.
examples.cn: 工程师正在测试一种有朝一日能让受损软骨再生的凝胶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡他力吉」（cartilage）——卡在两块硬骨之间、用力就变形的软垫 → 软骨

root: 拉丁 cartilago（属格 cartilaginis）「软骨、脆骨」，经古法语进入英语；其拉丁语内更深来源不确定，与 cratis「柳条编织物」或 caro「肉」的联系均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material: a firm but flexible pad. It appears as tissue, as a joint surface, as airway rings, as ear and nose shape, as a whole shark skeleton, as rib connectors, as a slow-healing tissue, and finally as gristle on a plate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种材料展开：坚实而有弹性的垫层。它依次呈现为组织、关节面、气道环、耳鼻外形、整副鲨鱼骨架、肋骨连接件、愈合缓慢的组织，最后是盘中难嚼的脆骨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flexible pad that keeps two hard things apart and lets them move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块有弹性的垫层，把两件硬物隔开，又让它们能够活动。

branches.en: PAD AND SURFACE: the tissue in general, and the smooth layer that takes friction at a joint.
branches.cn: 垫层与表面：泛指这种组织，以及关节处承受摩擦的光滑层。

branches.en: CONNECTOR AND FRAME: rings that hold an airway open, bars that tie ribs to the sternum.
branches.cn: 连接与支架：把气道撑开的环，把肋骨系到胸骨的条。

branches.en: ELASTICITY: an ear that springs back, and a whole animal framed in the same soft material.
branches.cn: 弹性：会弹回的耳朵，以及整副由同种软材料构成的动物骨架。

branches.en: NO BLOOD SUPPLY: without vessels, the pad cannot rebuild itself quickly.
branches.cn: 没有血供：没有血管，这块垫子就无法快速自我修复。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN VIEW: the same tissue is simply tough gristle when it reaches a plate.
branches.cn: 厨房视角：同一种组织到了盘子里，就只是难嚼的脆骨。

intro.en: Cartilage itself is a whole Latin noun rather than a prefixed form, but its stem and the Greek equivalent build the technical vocabulary of joints and skeleton.
intro.cn: cartilage 本身是一个完整的拉丁名词，并非前缀构词；但它的词干与希腊语对应词共同构成了关节与骨架的技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin cartilago gives the adjective cartilagineus; Greek chondros supplies the modern combining form chondro-, which medical English borrowed through scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cartilago 衍生形容词 cartilagineus；希腊 chondros 提供现代构词成分 chondro-，医学英语经科学拉丁语借入。

items.example: The Latin noun already named the flexible parts of the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已用来指身体中柔韧的部分。

items.meaning: made of or relating to cartilage
items.example: The shark has a cartilaginous skeleton.
Chondro- appears in the names of cartilage cells and fibres.
items.exampleCN: chondro- 出现在软骨细胞与纤维的名称中。

items.example: Chondrocytes sit in small spaces inside the matrix.
items.exampleCN: 软骨细胞位于基质中的小腔里。

items.meaning: a polysaccharide found in cartilage matrix
items.meaningCN: 软骨基质中的一种多糖
items.example: Chondroitin sulfate helps the matrix hold water.
items.exampleCN: 硫酸软骨素帮助基质保持水分。

items.meaning: cartilage reinforced with dense fibre bundles
items.meaningCN: 由密集纤维束加固的软骨
items.example: Fibrocartilage forms the pad inside the knee.
items.exampleCN: 纤维软骨构成膝关节内的垫层。

items.meaning: glassy, translucent cartilage of joint surfaces
items.meaningCN: 关节面上玻璃样、半透明的软骨
items.example: Hyaline cartilage covers the ends of long bones.
items.exampleCN: 透明软骨覆盖长骨的骨端。

items.meaningCN: 包在软骨外面的纤维层
items.example: The perichondrium supplies cells for new cartilage.
items.exampleCN: 软骨膜为新软骨提供细胞。

items.meaning: a piece of cartilage moved to repair another site
items.meaningCN: 移植到另一处进行修复的软骨块
items.example: The surgeon used a cartilage graft from the rib.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生使用了取自肋骨的软骨移植物。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 软骨；颗粒（拉丁医学文献沿用）

senses.title: A person who leaves to settle abroad

senses.definition: someone who departs from their own country in order to make a home in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国并打算在他国安家的人
senses.example: Every emigrant in the survey sent money home at least once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 调查中的每一位迁出者每年至少寄钱回家一次。
senses.why: the word is the person noun of the verb of leaving, so it names the one who has made the outward crossing.

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.definition: used attributively for ships, families, workers or communities connected with leaving
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，用于与离开有关的船只、家庭、工人或社群
senses.example: Emigrant ships left the harbour every week in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天每周都有移民船离开港口。
senses.why: English lets a person noun modify another noun without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许人称名词不加变化地修饰另一个名词。

senses.title: A political exile
senses.definition: a person who leaves because of persecution or political pressure rather than free choice
senses.definitionCN: 因迫害或政治压力而非自由选择而离开的人
senses.example: The poet lived as an emigrant in three capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人在三座首都以流亡者身份生活。
senses.why: the older word for a person who leaves has long covered those pushed out as well as those who choose to go.
senses.whyCN: 这个指离开者的旧词，长期以来既涵盖被逼走的人，也涵盖自愿离开的人。

senses.title: A contract labourer abroad
senses.definition: a worker who leaves to take a job in another country, often temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国到另一国工作的人，常为临时性
senses.example: Emigrant workers built the railway and then returned home.
senses.exampleCN: 外迁劳工修完铁路后回了家。
senses.why: labour demand turns the settler into a worker who may return, and the noun follows the person, not the intention.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力需求把定居者变成可能归来的工人，名词跟随的是人，而非意图。

senses.title: A person who returns
senses.definition: a former emigrant who comes back to the country of origin
senses.definitionCN: 回到原籍国的昔日迁出者
senses.example: Returning emigrants brought savings and new building styles.
senses.exampleCN: 归国的迁出者带回了积蓄与新的建筑样式。
senses.why: the label sticks to the person even after the move is reversed, which is why the returning form is needed.
senses.whyCN: 即使移动已经反向，这个标签仍跟着人，因此需要「归国的」这一说法。

senses.title: A community abroad
senses.definition: emigrants from one place considered together as a group in their new country
senses.definitionCN: 来自同一地方的迁出者在新国家作为整体来看
senses.example: The emigrant community funded a school in the old village.
senses.exampleCN: 海外侨民群体在老村资助了一所学校。
senses.why: a collection of individuals becomes a social body with its own institutions and money.
senses.whyCN: 个体的集合会变成拥有自身机构与资金的社会体。

senses.title: A dispersing organism
senses.definition: an individual that leaves a population to settle elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 离开原种群到他处立足的个体
senses.example: Each emigrant wolf must find unoccupied territory.
senses.exampleCN: 每一只迁出的狼都必须找到未被占据的领地。
senses.why: ecology borrows the human noun for the individual that leaves a group, matching the verb of departure.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个指人的名词，指离开群体的个体，与表离开的动词相配。

senses.title: A passenger-list category
senses.titleCN: 乘客名单上的登记类别
senses.definition: a person recorded under the heading of emigrants in shipping or border records
senses.definitionCN: 在航运或边境记录中以迁出者名目登记的人
senses.example: The archive lists him as an emigrant, though he later returned.
senses.exampleCN: 档案把他登记为迁出者，尽管他后来回来了。
senses.why: administrative records turn a moving person into a ticked box, and the box keeps its own name.
senses.whyCN: 行政记录把移动中的人变成一个勾选栏，而这个栏位保留了自己的名称。

intro.en: Emigrant is the present participle stem of Latin emigrare 'to move out', from e- 'out' plus migrare 'to migrate'. English took it from French in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: emigrant 是拉丁 emigrare「迁出」的现在分词词干，由 e-「向外」与 migrare「迁移」构成。英语在 18 世纪经法语吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move, change one's dwelling'. Its earlier origin is not established, and the root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「迁移、更换住所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，为其提出的词根属重构形式。

items.en: E- 'out' plus migrare gave emigrare 'to move out of a place'. Its participle emigrans named a person in the act of leaving.
items.cn: e-「向外」加 migrare 构成 emigrare「迁出某地」，其分词 emigrans 指正在离开的人。

items.en: French emigrant carried the participle into English as a noun, in the same period when immigration and emigration were settling into their modern pair.
items.cn: 法语 emigrant 把这个分词作为名词带入英语，正值迁入与迁出两个名词逐渐固定为现代配对之时。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun covered settlers, contract workers and political exiles alike.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，这个名词已同时涵盖定居者、合同劳工与政治流亡者。

items.en: Nineteenth-century passenger lists made the word a bureaucratic category, which is why the returning form later became necessary.
items.cn: 19 世纪的乘客名单使这个词成为官僚分类，这也是后来需要「归国的」这一说法的原因。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the direction words that differ by a single prefix; group two holds other names for people living away from home.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个前缀的方向词；第二组是对离家者的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The person at the receiving end of the same crossing; one individual is both an emigrant and an immigrant at once.
entries.definitionCN: 同一次越境在接收端的那个人；同一个人可以同时是迁出者与迁入者。

entries.definition: Anyone or anything that moves between places, with no prefix and no fixed direction; it also covers internal movement.
entries.definitionCN: 任何在各地之间移动的人或物，没有前缀也没有固定方向；也涵盖国内流动。

entries.definition: The act or flow of leaving, not a single person.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的行为或流量，不是单个人。

entries.definition: To move into a country; its prefix points at the destination rather than the origin.
entries.definitionCN: 移入某国；前缀指向目的地而非原籍。

entries.definition: A person living outside their own country, often for work; the word usually implies choice and a continuing link home.
entries.definitionCN: 居住在国外的人，常因工作；通常暗示自愿选择并保持与家乡的联系。

entries.definition: A person forced to live away from home, or the state of being so forced; compulsion is central.
entries.definitionCN: 被迫离家居住的人，或这种状态；强迫性是核心。

entries.definition: A person outside their country because of war or persecution, with a legal status that emigrant does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 因战争或迫害而身在他国的人，拥有迁出者一词所不包含的法律身份。

entries.definition: A person who takes up land and builds a permanent home, seen from the destination rather than the departure.
entries.definitionCN: 占据土地并建立永久居所的人，从目的地而非出发地来看。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means out: the emigrant is the one walking away from the gate.
normal.cn: 前缀意为向外：迁出者就是走出闸口的那个人。

normal.en: The pair emigrant and immigrant differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 迁出者与迁入者这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun ends in a suffix marking the one who acts.
normal.cn: 指人的名词以一个标记施动者的词尾收束。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as emigrant ship and emigrant community belong to the historical and social senses.
normal.cn: 移民船、海外侨民社群这类固定搭配属于历史与社会义。

normal.en: In ecology the same noun names an individual that leaves its pack.
normal.cn: 在生态学中，同一个名词指离开群体的个体。

abstract.en: Picture a single ticket that has no return half.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有回程联的单程票。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph left behind in a drawer on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被故意留在抽屉里的全家福。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from a house outward, with the house still visible at its tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从房屋画出的箭头，箭尾仍看得见那所房子。

examples.en: The emigrant sent a third of his wages to his parents every month.
examples.cn: 这位迁出者每月把三分之一的工资寄给父母。

examples.en: Emigrant associations raised money for schools back home.
examples.cn: 迁出者协会为家乡的学校筹款。

examples.en: The museum displays letters written by emigrants on the voyage.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出迁出者在航程中写的信件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·出去」——一个人离开本国去别处定居，就是迁出者

root: 拉丁 e-「向外」+ migrare「迁移」→ emigrare「迁出」，取其现在分词词干加人称词尾得 emigrant。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person at the gate: the one who leaves to settle abroad, a modifier before a noun, an exile, a contract worker, one who returns, a community abroad, a dispersing animal and a box ticked on a passenger list.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕闸口前的同一个人展开：离开并到国外定居的人、名词前的修饰语、流亡者、合同劳工、归国者、海外社群、扩散的动物，以及乘客名单上被勾选的一栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller at the departure gate holding a one-way ticket.
core.cn: 核心意象：出境闸口前一名旅客握着单程票。

branches.en: THE LEAVER: the base sense, the person who departs in order to settle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 离开者：基础义，为在别处定居而出走的人。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the noun doubles as a modifier in fixed phrases.
branches.cn: 语法：这个名词在固定搭配中兼作修饰语。

branches.en: MOTIVE: persecution pushes some out, and work pulls others away.
branches.cn: 动机：迫害把一些人推走，工作把另一些人拉走。

branches.en: AFTERWARD: the label persists through a return, and a crowd of leavers becomes a community abroad.
branches.cn: 之后：标签在人归国后仍然跟着，而一群离开者会在海外成为社群。

branches.en: NATURE AND PAPER: an animal dispersing, and a name entered in a shipping ledger.
branches.cn: 自然与纸面：扩散的动物，以及写进航运登记簿的名字。

intro.en: Emigrant is a prefix, a root and a person suffix, and the same pieces build the migration family.
intro.cn: emigrant 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个表人后缀构成，同样的成分构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin e- marks motion outward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and the participle ending -ant names the person doing it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 e- 标记向外移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，分词词尾 -ant 为做这件事的人命名。

items.example: The prefix points away from the home country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指向远离故土的方向。

items.example: The root carries the idea of moving home.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着搬迁的意思。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: They emigrated after the factory closed.
It builds the person noun from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成指人的名词。
这位迁出者只带了一只箱子。

items.example: It names the process rather than the person.
Emigration reduced the village to half its size.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民使这个村子只剩一半人口。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这一过程的形容词。

items.example: The emigratory route ran through the port.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民的路线经过这个港口。

items.example: Migration may be seasonal or permanent.
items.exampleCN: 迁移可以是季节性的，也可以是永久的。

definition_zh: 推测的；猜测性的；投机性的（金融上指高风险、指望价差获利）
definition_en: based on guesswork rather than firm evidence, or carrying a high financial risk in the hope of a large gain
core_image: 一张尚未完工的蓝图压在几枚硬币下面，图纸边角还写着几个问号

sceneCN: 这里指「建立在猜测而非确证之上的」（第 1 个义项：结论依赖未经验证的假设）；句意为分析师写了三页「可能」与「如果」，最后承认这些结论都只是推测性的。可辨识物件：未完工的蓝图、硬币、问号、批注笔。
