senses.title: Resting on guesswork
senses.definition: formed from conjecture rather than from proof or direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 由猜测而非证明或直接观察形成
senses.example: The dating of the layer remains speculative until the pottery is analysed.
senses.exampleCN: 在陶器完成分析之前，这一地层的年代仍是推测性的。
senses.why: the adjective adds a quality to the act of guessing, so it describes any claim whose support is not yet there.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词给「猜测」这一动作加上性质，因此描述任何尚缺支撑的主张。

senses.title: Financially risky in pursuit of gain
senses.titleCN: 为求收益而承担高金融风险
senses.definition: describing an investment whose return depends on an expected price change and may easily be lost
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种收益取决于预期价差、且很可能全部损失的投资
senses.example: Regulators warned that the new fund was too speculative for small savers.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构警告说，这只新基金对小型储户来说投机性太强。
senses.why: in finance the quality is attached to the position rather than the theory: the guess is now backed by money.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，这一性质附着于头寸而非理论：猜测此时已由金钱背书。

senses.title: Purely theoretical inquiry
senses.definition: concerned with reasoning about matters that cannot be settled by experiment
senses.definitionCN: 关心无法用实验定论的问题的推理
senses.example: Medieval scholars divided speculative philosophy from practical ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪学者把思辨哲学与实践伦理分开。
senses.why: the old academic sense treats speculation as an honourable activity, so the adjective marks thought that seeks truth rather than use.
senses.whyCN: 古老的学术义把思辨视为体面活动，因此这个形容词标记「求真理而非求实用」的思考。

senses.title: A mind inclined to guess
senses.definition: describing a person whose habit is to form conclusions quickly on limited grounds
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个人习惯凭有限依据迅速下结论
senses.example: He has a speculative turn of mind and trusts his hunches too soon.
senses.exampleCN: 他天性爱推测，对自己的直觉信得太快。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the person as well as the claim, which is why it also names a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述主张，也能描述人，因此也指一种性情。

senses.title: Speculative fiction as a genre
senses.definition: naming stories that invent worlds beyond the present one, such as science fiction and fantasy
senses.definitionCN: 指发明超越当下世界的叙事，如科幻与奇幻
senses.example: The course reads speculative fiction alongside the history of technology.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把推想小说与技术史放在一起读。
senses.why: the genre label extends the idea of imagining what is not yet here from markets to whole invented worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这一文类标签把「想象尚未存在之物」从市场扩展到整个虚构世界。

senses.title: An unsolicited speculative approach
senses.titleCN: 未经邀约的试探性申请
senses.definition: describing a job application or business inquiry sent without an advertised opening
senses.definitionCN: 描述在没有公开招聘时主动寄出的求职申请或商业询问
senses.example: She sent a speculative application to the publisher and got a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 她向这家出版社寄了一份试探性申请，并收到了回复。
senses.why: because nothing has been offered yet, the approach itself is a guess that a place might exist.
senses.whyCN: 因为对方尚未提供职位，这种主动接触本身就是「也许有空缺」的猜测。

senses.title: Describing an inflated asset price
senses.titleCN: 描述被吹高的资产价格
senses.definition: describing prices that have risen because buyers expect further rises rather than because of earnings
senses.definitionCN: 描述因买者预期继续上涨、而非因盈利上升而抬高的价格
senses.example: The land market turned speculative long before construction began.
senses.exampleCN: 早在地基动工之前，土地市场就已变得投机化。
senses.why: when a whole market takes on the quality, the adjective shifts from one trade to the level of prices.
senses.whyCN: 当整个市场带上这种性质，形容词就从单笔交易转到价格水平。

senses.title: The speculative motive in economics
senses.definition: naming the reason to hold cash or an asset because its price is expected to change favourably
senses.definitionCN: 指因预期价格将有利变化而持有现金或资产的理由
senses.example: Keynes treated the speculative motive as one of three reasons for holding money.
senses.exampleCN: 凯恩斯把投机动机视为持有货币的三种理由之一。
senses.why: economics turned the adjective into a named category of behaviour, which is its most technical use.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这个形容词变成一个有名字的行为类别，这是其最技术的用法。

intro.en: Speculative is the Latin-derived adjective of speculation: speculativus came from speculari 'to watch', and English took it through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: speculative 是 speculation 的拉丁系形容词：speculativus 出自 speculari「观察」，英语经法语吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Speculari meant 'to watch from a height, to spy, to examine'. The adjective speculativus was formed on its participial stem.
items.cn: speculari 意为「从高处观察、窥探、审视」。形容词 speculativus 即在其分词词干上构成。

items.en: In later Latin, speculativus described matters belonging to contemplation rather than to action, a division inherited from Greek philosophy.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，speculativus 描述属于沉思而非行动的事物，这一区分承自希腊哲学。

items.en: Medieval schools paired speculative with practical, meaning the one seeks knowledge and the other guides conduct.
items.cn: 中世纪学校把「思辨的」与「实践的」配对，前者求知识，后者指导行为。

items.en: The adjective reached English in the fifteenth century by way of French speculatif, keeping the scholarly sense of contemplative.
items.cn: 这个形容词于 15 世纪经法语 speculatif 进入英语，保留了「沉思的」学术义。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the same adjective was applied to ventures resting on expected prices, and the financial sense became dominant.
items.cn: 在 18 与 19 世纪，同一形容词被用于依赖预期价格的事业，金融义遂占主导。

items.en: The twentieth century added speculative fiction as a genre label and speculative application as a polite name for an unsolicited approach.
items.cn: 20 世纪又添上「推想小说」的文类标签，以及作为「主动投递」委婉说法的试探性申请。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and its look-alikes; group two holds adjectives that also mean uncertain or risky, with different grounds.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词族与形近词；第二组是同样表示不确定或有风险的其他形容词，各自依据不同。

entries.definition: The act or content of guessing; the adjective describes how well founded a claim or position is.
entries.definitionCN: 指猜测的动作或内容；形容词描述主张或头寸的可靠程度。

entries.definition: To form a guess or to take a price bet; the adjective is what such an act produces or embodies.
entries.definitionCN: 指作出猜测或押注价格；形容词是这样的动作产生或体现的性质。

entries.definition: The agent who speculates; the adjective does not name a person unless a noun follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行投机的人；形容词若不接名词则不指人。

entries.definition: From spectare 'to view': striking to look at. It shares the root but not the guessing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自「观看」：指视觉上引人注目。它共享词根，但与猜测无关。

entries.definition: Resting on inference from incomplete evidence; it sounds more formal and less financial than speculative.
entries.definitionCN: 指依据不完整证据的推断；比 speculative 更书面、更少金融色彩。

entries.definition: Offered as a first attempt that may be revised; it stresses caution, not the hope of gain.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为可能修改的初次尝试；强调谨慎，而非指望收益。

entries.definition: Carrying the chance of loss; speculative adds the expectation of a reward that justifies the risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有损失可能；speculative 另含「有值得冒险的预期收益」。

entries.definition: Put forward as a supposition to be tested or explored; it need not involve money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为待检验或探讨的假设提出；未必涉及金钱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Same tower, now as a quality: whatever is seen from it is seen imperfectly, so the conclusion is a guess.
normal.cn: 同一座塔，现在化作品质：从塔上看到的东西都不完整，所以结论只是猜测。

normal.en: The family runs speculate, speculation, speculative, speculator, speculatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括推测、猜测、推测性的、投机者、凭推测地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: speculative investment, speculative bubble, speculative fiction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：投机性投资、投机泡沫、推想小说。

normal.en: The scholarly pair is speculative and practical: one seeks truth, the other guides action.
normal.cn: 学术上的配对是「思辨的」与「实践的」：前者求真理，后者指导行动。

normal.en: A speculative application guesses that a job exists before it is advertised.
normal.cn: 试探性申请是在职位公开招聘之前就猜它存在。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint with coins set on its corners and question marks pencilled in the margins.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图，四角压着硬币，页边用铅笔写着问号。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge over fog, walked because the other side might be rich.
abstract.cn: 想象一座雾中的绳桥，人愿意走上去，只因对岸也许富庶。

abstract.en: Picture a novelist drawing a map of a country that has never existed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位小说家画出一个从未存在过的国家的地图。

examples.en: Any estimate of the storm's path this early is speculative.
examples.cn: 这么早对风暴路径作任何估计都只是推测。

examples.en: The fund attracted speculative money that vanished when rates rose.
examples.cn: 这只基金吸引了投机资金，利率上升后这些钱便消失了。

examples.en: His speculative turn of mind made him a good theorist and a poor treasurer.
examples.cn: 他爱推测的性格让他成为好的理论家、糟糕的司库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看」的词根加形容词后缀——只凭远远看一眼就下结论，这样的结论就是推测性的；拿钱去赌这个结论就是投机性的

root: 拉丁 speculativus 出自 speculari「观察」（specula「瞭望塔」+ specere「看」），经法语 speculatif 入英语；同根词有 inspect、spectacle、perspective。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a quality rather than an act: a claim, a position, a discipline, a temperament, a genre, an approach, a price level and a motive are each said to rest on something not yet seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是性质而非动作：主张、头寸、学科、性情、文类、接触方式、价格水平与动机，各自被说成建立在尚未看见的东西上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conclusion built on a view from far off, with the missing part left blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：建立在远望之上的结论，缺失的部分留成空白。

branches.en: THEORY AND CONTEMPLATION: the oldest layer is a claim or a discipline that seeks truth without proof.
branches.cn: 理论与沉思：最古老的一层是求真理而无证明的主张或学科。

branches.en: MONEY AND PRICES: the guess is backed by capital, then colours a whole market level.
branches.cn: 金钱与价格：猜测由资本背书，进而染及整个市场价格水平。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same quality settles into a temperament that trusts hunches.
branches.cn: 人：同一性质沉淀为信赖直觉的性情。

branches.en: INVENTED WORLDS: imagining what does not exist is extended from markets to fiction.
branches.cn: 虚构世界：对不存在之物的想象从市场延伸到小说。

branches.en: APPROACH AND MOTIVE: an unsolicited contact and a reason to hold cash both assume a future that may not come.
branches.cn: 接触与动机：主动投递与持有现金的理由，都预设一个未必到来的未来。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin root for looking plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'; it describes whatever leans on a view rather than on proof.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是「看」的拉丁词根加「倾向于」的后缀；它描述任何依赖视野而非证据的事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look' gives specula and speculari, whose adjective speculativus becomes English speculative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 specere「看」给出瞭望塔与观察，其形容词 speculativus 变成英语的 speculative。

items.example: The root is about seeing, not proving.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根关乎看见，而非证明。

items.example: The tower supplies the distance in the word.
items.exampleCN: 那座塔提供了词中的距离感。

items.example: The verb adds intent to the look.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给「看」加上意图。

items.example: Medieval schools used it for pure theory.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪学校用它指纯理论。

items.example: The noun names the act behind the quality.
items.exampleCN: 名词指这一性质背后的动作。

items.meaning: to guess; to trade on price
items.exampleCN: 他们推测下一季度的情况。

items.example: The speculator sold before the crash.
items.exampleCN: 这名投机者在崩盘前卖出。

items.meaning: tending to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns an act into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成性质。

items.example: From the ridge the perspective opens.

definition_zh: n. 心绞痛（心肌缺血引起的胸痛）；咽峡炎
definition_en: Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle; in older medical use, a severe choking sore throat.
core_image: 胸口被一只看不见的手攥住
scene: 他爬到三楼就得停下，胸口发紧。 The doctor diagnosed angina after the stress test.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：爬楼时胸口发紧、休息后缓解，是心肌供血不足引起的心绞痛，医学上称 angina。

derivatives.zh: 心绞痛的
胸部的（拉丁语属格）
咽峡炎的

senses.title: Chest pain from a short of blood
senses.definition: a squeezing chest pain that appears when the heart muscle does not get enough blood, usually on effort
senses.definitionCN: 心肌供血不足时出现的压榨性胸痛，通常在用力时发作
senses.example: The angina eased once he sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 他一坐下，心绞痛就缓解了。
senses.why: Latin angina meant a choking sore throat, from a root meaning to squeeze; the heart sense keeps the same image of a tightening grip.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angina 意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，出自意为「挤压」的词根；心脏义保留了同一幅「被攥紧」的画面。

senses.title: The older throat sense
senses.definition: a severe sore throat with swelling that threatens the airway, as in quinsy
senses.definitionCN: 伴肿胀并威胁气道的严重咽痛，如扁桃体周围脓肿
senses.example: The old texts use angina for a strangling throat infection.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献用 angina 指一种令人窒息的喉部感染。
senses.why: This is the original sense: before cardiology borrowed the word, angina named any condition that felt like being strangled.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：在心脏病学借用该词之前，angina 指任何感觉像被勒住的病症。

intro.en: Angina is Latin for a choking sore throat, from Greek ankhonē, strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze. Heberden added pectoris, of the chest, in 1768 and the modern heart sense was fixed.
intro.cn: angina 在拉丁语中意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，来自希腊语 ankhonē「勒紧」，后者出自 ankhein「挤压」。赫伯登 1768 年加上 pectoris「胸部的」，现代心脏义由此确定。

items.en: Greek ankhonē meant strangling or a strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze tight. The physical image is a hand closing on the throat.
items.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 意为「勒紧、窒息」，来自 ankhein「紧紧挤压」。身体意象是一只手扣住喉咙。

items.en: Latin angina named a severe sore throat, especially quinsy, and belongs to the same family as angere, to choke, which gives anxious and anger.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angina 指严重咽痛，尤指扁桃体周围脓肿，与 angere「使窒息」同族，后者产生 anxious 与 anger。

items.en: William Heberden described the chest condition in 1768 and called it angina pectoris, angina of the chest, to separate it from the throat disease.
items.cn: 赫伯登 1768 年描述了这种胸部病症，称其为 angina pectoris「胸部绞痛」，以与喉部疾病区分。

items.en: English took angina in the sixteenth century for the throat sense, and the cardiac meaning spread only after Heberden named it.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 angina 指咽喉义，心脏义在赫伯登命名之后才传播开来。

items.en: In current medicine angina alone almost always means the heart condition, and the throat sense survives mainly in older texts.
items.cn: 在当代医学中，单独的 angina 几乎总指心脏病症，咽喉义主要保存在旧文献中。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the squeeze family angina, anguish, anger and anxious; the near-meaning group lists related conditions.
note.cn: 形近组保留「挤压」词族 angina、anguish、anger、anxious；近义组列出相关病症。

entries.definition: Severe mental or physical suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的精神或肉体痛苦。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of displeasure.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的不快情绪。

entries.definition: Worried and uneasy.
entries.definitionCN: 担忧而不安的。

entries.definition: Relating to angina.
entries.definitionCN: 与心绞痛有关的。

entries.definition: A reduced blood supply to a tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 某组织供血减少。

entries.definition: Tissue death from a blocked supply.
entries.definitionCN: 供血受阻导致的组织坏死。

entries.definition: An abscess beside the tonsil.
entries.definitionCN: 扁桃体旁的脓肿。

entries.definition: A sudden tight muscle pain.
entries.definitionCN: 突发的肌肉紧缩痛。

normalIntro.en: Angina shares a root with anger and anguish: all three come from a squeezing grip.
normalIntro.cn: angina 与 anger、anguish 同根：三者都来自「被攥紧」这个动作。

normal.en: Angina pectoris is the full name; pectoris means of the chest.
normal.cn: angina pectoris 是全称，pectoris 意为「胸部的」。

normal.en: It is uncountable: angina, not an angina, though an angina attack is fine.
normal.cn: 它不可数：angina，不说 an angina，但 an angina attack 可以。

normal.en: Stable angina comes on effort; unstable angina comes at rest.
normal.cn: 稳定型心绞痛在用力时发作，不稳定型在静息时发作。

normal.en: Do not confuse angina with anguish, which is suffering in general.
normal.cn: 别把 angina 与 anguish 混淆，后者泛指痛苦。

normal.en: The adjective is anginal, as in anginal pain.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anginal，如 anginal pain。

abstract.en: Picture a fist tightening behind the breastbone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头在胸骨后收紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a staircase that has to be climbed in stages.
abstract.cn: 想象一段必须分几次爬完的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of a pipe narrowed until the flow slows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被收窄到水流变慢的管子。

examples.en: He carries tablets for his angina in his coat pocket.
examples.cn: 他外套口袋里装着治心绞痛的药片。

examples.en: The scan showed no sign of angina at rest.
examples.cn: 扫描显示静息时没有心绞痛迹象。

examples.en: Angina pectoris was first described in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 心绞痛最早在 18 世纪被描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安绞痛」——安（an）绞（gi）痛（na）：安静下来才不绞痛，一用力就攥住胸口，就是心绞痛。

root: 希腊语 ankhein「挤压」生出 ankhonē「勒紧」，拉丁语作 angina 指窒息性咽痛；赫伯登 1768 年加 pectoris「胸部的」，遂指心肌缺血性胸痛。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one grip: the older strangling throat infection, and the modern squeezing pain of a heart short of blood.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次攥紧：较早的窒息性喉部感染，以及现代心脏缺血时的压榨性疼痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible hand tightening on the chest
core.cn: 核心意象：一只看不见的手在胸口收紧

branches.en: A tight chest on the third flight of stairs.
branches.cn: 爬到第三层楼梯时发紧的胸口。

branches.en: Pain that fades when the walk stops.
branches.cn: 停下脚步就消退的疼痛。

branches.en: A swollen throat that barely lets air through.
branches.cn: 肿到几乎不通气的喉咙。

branches.en: An old case note naming quinsy.
branches.cn: 一份写着扁桃体脓肿的旧病历。

branches.en: Both feel like being strangled.
branches.cn: 两者都像被勒住。

intro.en: Angina carries the squeeze root ang-, which also builds anger, anxious and anguish.
intro.cn: angina 带着「挤压」词根 ang-，这个词根还构成 anger、anxious 与 anguish。

latinIntro.en: Greek ankhonē became Latin angina; the same Latin angere, to choke, gives anxious and anger, so the family is easy to keep together.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 变成拉丁语 angina；同一个拉丁语 angere「使窒息」产生 anxious 与 anger，所以这个词族很容易一起记。

latinEntries.example: Angina first named the throat disease.

latinEntries.exampleCN: angere 产生 anxious 与 anger。

definition_zh: 使适应（新环境）；服水土
definition_en: to become used to a new place, climate, or situation
core_image: 候鸟落在新枝头：一点点调整自己融入新环境
scene: 高原的新兵头几天喘不上气，两周后已能轻松跑完全程。 It took him weeks to acclimate to the high altitude.
sceneCN: 这里 acclimate 是「适应新环境」（第 1 个义项：让身体习惯新条件）；句意为他花了几周才适应高原环境。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「适应；服水土」
同源变体，义为「使适应气候」

senses.title: To adjust to a climate or place
senses.definition: to let body or mind become used to new surroundings or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 让身体或心理习惯新的环境或条件
senses.example: The plants acclimated quickly to the greenhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物很快适应了温室环境。
senses.why: The word was first used of plants and climate; the core idea is a living thing settling into new conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初用于植物与气候；核心观念是生命体在新条件中安顿下来。

senses.title: To adjust to a new situation
senses.definition: to become comfortable in a new job, culture, or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 在新工作、文化或生活方式中变得自在
senses.example: New hires usually acclimate within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工通常一个月内就能适应。
senses.why: If a body can settle into new weather, a mind can settle into new circumstances, so the word stretched to life changes.
senses.whyCN: 身体能安顿于新天气，心理也能安顿于新境遇，于是这个词扩展到生活变化。

intro.en: Acclimate is a French-style blend of acclimatize, joining ad- 'toward' with climat 'climate'.
intro.cn: acclimate 是 acclimatize 的法语式简化，由 ad-（向）与 climat（气候）拼合。

items.en: klima meant the slope of the ground, later its weather zone.
items.cn: 希腊语 klima 指地面的坡度，后指其气候带。

items.en: French climat narrowed to mean weather conditions.
items.cn: 法语 climat 收窄为指天气状况。

items.en: acclimater meant to habituate to a climate.
items.cn: 法语 acclimater 意为使习惯于某气候。

items.en: English formed acclimatize in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪造出 acclimatize。

items.en: The shorter acclimate is now standard American usage.
items.cn: 较短的 acclimate 是如今美式标准用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the climate word family; the second gathers verbs for adapting.
note.cn: 第一组收气候词族；第二组收表示适应的动词。

entries.definition: The longer British-style variant of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的较长英式变体。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of adapting.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指适应的过程。

entries.definition: The usual weather of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指一地的气候。

entries.definition: To change oneself to fit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应；改造自己以配合新条件」。

entries.definition: To make small changes to fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整以适应」。

entries.definition: To make used to something by repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 书面语动词，义为「使习惯于」。

entries.definition: To become comfortable in a new home or place.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「安顿下来」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the climate root and the a- prefix; the abstract hooks picture gradual settling.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 climate 词根与前缀 a-；抽象记忆点想象逐步安顿的过程。

normal.en: See climate inside the word: the core meaning is adjusting to climate.
normal.cn: 词中有 climate：核心义就是适应气候。

normal.en: A- is a reduced form of ad-, meaning toward.
normal.cn: a- 是 ad- 的弱化形式，意为「向」。

normal.en: Acclimatize is the longer British twin of acclimate.
normal.cn: acclimatize 是 acclimate 较长的英式孪生词。

normal.en: The noun acclimation names the settling process.
normal.cn: 名词 acclimation 指安顿适应的过程。

normal.en: Both people and plants can acclimate.
normal.cn: 人和植物都可以 acclimate。

abstract.en: Picture a transplanted tree slowly growing new roots.
abstract.cn: 想象移栽的树慢慢长出新根。

abstract.en: Picture a climber pausing each day to let the mountain feel normal.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者每天停一停，让高海拔慢慢变得平常。

abstract.en: Picture a new student finding their seat in an unfamiliar hall.
abstract.cn: 想象新生在陌生礼堂里找到自己的位置。

examples.en: A month in the city was enough to acclimate her to the noise.
examples.cn: 在城里待上一个月就足以让她适应噪音。

examples.en: Farmers acclimate seedlings before planting them outdoors.
examples.cn: 农民在把幼苗移到户外前先让它们适应环境。

examples.en: It is easier to acclimate when you keep a routine.
examples.cn: 保持作息规律更容易适应新环境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克克里买特」——到了新地方先「买」点当地的「特」产，慢慢就习惯了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ 希腊语 klima 经法语 climat（气候）→ acclimater（使习惯于气候）→ 英语 acclimate（使适应）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from adjusting to a physical climate, to adjusting to any new situation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从适应自然气候，扩展到适应任何新处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living thing slowly rooting into new conditions
core.cn: 核心意象：生命体慢慢在新条件中扎根

branches.en: Body or plant settling into new air and weather.
branches.cn: 身体或植物在新空气与天气中安顿。

branches.en: Mind settling into new work or culture.
branches.cn: 心理在新工作或文化中安顿。

branches.en: Both senses are the same settling at different depths.
branches.cn: 两个义项是同一种安顿在不同层面的体现。

branches.en: Adjustment takes time and gentle repetition.
branches.cn: 适应需要时间与温和的重复。

branches.en: Comfort grows as the unfamiliar turns routine.
branches.cn: 当陌生变成日常，自在随之生长。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the climate stem and a verb ending; the family adds a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「气候」词干与动词结尾组成；词族另派生名词。

latinIntro.en: The climate stem travelled through Latin and French, so the Latin entry records the borrowed noun.
latinIntro.cn: 「气候」词干经拉丁语与法语传播，拉丁条目记录借入的名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「适应；服水土」
动词，义为「使适应气候」

definition_zh: 隔离、扣押、封存（把某物分开并另行保管的行为；法律、财政、医学与气候语境各有专指）
definition_en: the act of setting something apart and keeping it in safekeeping, with specialised meanings in law, budgeting, medicine and climate policy
core_image: 一件有争议的财物被锁进第三方的柜子，钥匙不在当事人手里；同一动作移到陪审团、病人或预算上，各自成了一种隔离
scene: 法庭上法官下令把陪审团与外界隔开，以免他们读到案情报道。 The sequestration of the jury kept them away from news reports during the trial.
sceneCN: 这里 sequestration 指「把陪审团与外界隔离」（第 2 个义项：陪审团隔离）；句意为对陪审团的隔离使他们在庭审期间接触不到新闻报道。

pos.zh: 隔离；扣押；封存（可数指一次具体隔离，不可数指行为本身）

derivatives.zh: sequester（拉丁「受托人」）→ 隔离、扣押、封存：把某物放到别处保管
sequestrare（拉丁「另行保管」）的英语动词形 → 依法扣押：法律上的强制隔离
sequestrate + -ed（过去分词形容词）→ 被扣押的：处于强制保管状态
sequestrum（拉丁「寄存物」）→ 死骨片：与健康骨分离的一块骨
sequestrum + -otomy（希腊「切开」）→ 死骨切除术

senses.title: Setting something apart
senses.definition: the general act of separating a thing from ordinary use and holding it elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从日常使用中分出、另存他处的总称
senses.example: Sequestration in its oldest sense simply means setting a disputed thing aside.
senses.exampleCN: sequestration 最古老的含义只是把有争议的东西另行放置。
senses.why: every specialised sense keeps this core move: separation plus custody.
senses.whyCN: 每个专门义项都保留这个核心动作：分开加保管。

senses.title: Jury isolation
senses.definition: the confinement of jurors away from public contact and news during a trial
senses.definitionCN: 庭审期间让陪审员与公众接触和新闻隔绝
senses.example: The sequestration of the jury kept them away from news reports during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 对陪审团的隔离使他们在庭审期间接触不到新闻报道。
senses.why: a verdict must rest only on evidence heard in court, so the jury is physically set apart.
senses.whyCN: 裁决必须只依据庭上听到的证据，因此陪审团被物理地隔开。

senses.title: Property in custody
senses.definition: the legal holding of disputed property by a third party until a case is decided
senses.definitionCN: 案件裁断前由第三方保管争议财产
senses.example: A sequestration order froze the company's accounts during the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 一项扣押令在争议期间冻结了公司的账户。
senses.why: the word began as a trustee holding property, so the legal sense is the ancestral one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指受托保管财产的受托人，因此法律义项是它的祖义。

senses.title: Automatic budget cuts
senses.definition: mandatory across-the-board spending reductions triggered when budget limits are breached
senses.definitionCN: 预算上限被突破时触发的强制性全面开支削减
senses.example: Budget sequestration cut both defence and domestic programmes.
senses.exampleCN: 预算自动削减同时砍掉了国防与国内项目。
senses.why: the money is set aside by rule rather than by negotiation, which is exactly the old legal move applied to a treasury.
senses.whyCN: 这笔钱按规则而非谈判被扣下，正是古老的法律动作用在国库上。

senses.title: The lung anomaly
senses.definition: a congenital mass of lung tissue that has no normal connection to the airway
senses.definitionCN: 一块与气道没有正常连接的先天性肺组织
senses.example: Pulmonary sequestration is usually found on one side of the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 肺隔离症通常见于胸腔的一侧。
senses.why: the tissue is literally separated from the airway it should serve, so medicine borrowed the word for anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 那块组织确实与它本该服务的气道分开，因此医学借用了这个词来指解剖。

senses.title: Chemical binding
senses.definition: the locking of an ion or compound into a stable complex so it cannot react freely
senses.definitionCN: 把离子或化合物锁进稳定络合物使其不能自由反应
senses.example: Chemical sequestration of metals reduces their toxicity in soil.
senses.exampleCN: 金属的化学固定降低了它们在土壤中的毒性。
senses.why: the substance is held by another molecule the way property is held by a trustee.
senses.whyCN: 物质被另一个分子握住，就像财产被受托人保管。

senses.title: Carbon sequestration
senses.definition: the removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and its long-term storage
senses.definitionCN: 把二氧化碳从大气中移除并长期储存
senses.example: Carbon sequestration is counted only if the storage lasts for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 碳封存只有在储存延续数百年时才被计入。
senses.why: the climate sense applies the legal idea to a gas: take it out of circulation and put it under guard.
senses.whyCN: 气候义项把法律观念用在气体上：让它退出循环并置于看管之下。

senses.title: Ecclesiastical holding
senses.definition: the temporary transfer of a benefice or church income to another custodian
senses.definitionCN: 把教职俸禄或教会收入临时交给另一位代管人
senses.example: The sequestration of the parish income lasted until a new priest was appointed.
senses.exampleCN: 该堂区收入的代管一直持续到新司铎被任命。
senses.why: church law inherited the Roman idea of a neutral custodian for property in dispute.
senses.whyCN: 教会法继承了罗马法为争议财产设中立保管人的观念。

senses.title: Being cut off
senses.definition: a figurative condition of isolation or withdrawal from normal relations
senses.definitionCN: 与正常联系相隔绝的比喻状态
senses.example: The sequestration of the village by snow left it outside all supply routes.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪对村庄的隔绝使它脱离了所有补给路线。
senses.why: the core image survives in plain speech whenever something is shut away from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 只要有某物被隔开在其余之外，这个核心意象就在日常语言中存活。

intro.en: Sequestration comes from Latin sequestrare 'to set aside, to give into custody', built on sequester, a trustee or mediator who held disputed property. The deeper origin of sequester is uncertain (source uncertain), and it is generally thought to be related to sequi 'to follow'. English took the word in the fifteenth century as a legal term.
intro.cn: sequestration 来自拉丁 sequestrare「另行放置、交付保管」，其词基 sequester 指保管争议财产的受托人或中间人。sequester 的更早来源不确定，一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。英语于十五世纪作为法律术语借入。

items.en: A sequester was a neutral party who held property while a dispute was pending; its deeper origin is uncertain (source uncertain), and it is generally thought to be related to sequi 'to follow'.
items.cn: sequester 是在争议未决时保管财产的中立方；其更早来源不确定，一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。

items.en: The verb meant to separate a thing and place it in safe keeping, a procedural act of Roman law.
items.cn: 这个动词意为把某物分开并放到安全保管处，是罗马法中的程序性动作。

items.en: Sequestration entered English as the setting aside of disputed property or church income.
items.cn: sequestration 进入英语时指把争议财产或教会收入另行保管。

items.en: The word was extended to the isolation of jurors, applying custody to people rather than goods.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到陪审员的隔离，把保管的对象从财物变成人。

items.en: Sequestrum named a fragment of dead bone separated from healthy tissue, and pulmonary sequestration followed.
items.cn: sequestrum 指与健康组织分离的死骨片，肺隔离症之名随后出现。

items.en: American budget law revived the word for automatic spending cuts, and climate policy borrowed it again for carbon storage.
items.cn: 美国预算法律用这个词指自动削减开支，气候政策随后又借它指碳储存。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike forms of the same Latin family; group two holds the general words for isolating and impounding.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族的形近形式；第二组是表示隔离与扣押的一般词。

entries.definition: To set aside or isolate, especially carbon or funds; the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物另行放置或隔离，尤指碳或资金；名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: To take legal possession of property until a debt or dispute is settled; narrower than sequestration.
entries.definitionCN: 在债务或争议解决前依法占有财产；比 sequestration 窄。

entries.definition: A piece of dead bone separated from living bone; a single anatomical object, not a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 与活骨分离的死骨片；是一个解剖对象，不是政策。

entries.definition: Being cut off from contact; it names the condition, while sequestration names an imposed procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 与接触相隔绝；它命名状态，而 sequestration 命名一种强制程序。

entries.definition: Seizing property outright, usually by the state; sequestration holds it in custody rather than keeping it.
entries.definitionCN: 直接没收财产，通常由国家执行；sequestration 是保管而非占为己有。

entries.definition: The taking and holding of goods, vehicles or water; it is a physical or legal hold, not a budget rule.
entries.definitionCN: 扣留货物、车辆或水；是物理或法律上的扣住，不是预算规则。

entries.definition: The separation of people or animals to prevent contagion; it is a public-health subtype of isolation.
entries.definitionCN: 为防止传染而隔离人或动物；它是隔离的公共卫生子类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin legal root and the real chain of borrowed senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁法律词根，以及真实的一串借用义项。

normal.en: A sequester was a trustee: someone who held what others fought over.
normal.cn: sequester 曾是受托人：保管他人争夺之物的人。

normal.en: The pattern never changes: separate the thing, then keep it under guard.
normal.cn: 模式从未改变：先把东西分开，再置于看管之下。

normal.en: Property, jury, budget, bone, metal, gas: one verb, six stages of custody.
normal.cn: 财产、陪审团、预算、骨头、金属、气体：一个动词，六种保管。

normal.en: In climate text the bare word usually means carbon, so check the context.
normal.cn: 在气候文本里，单独这个词通常指碳，所以要看清上下文。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the act into a noun, as in fixation and isolation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ation 把动作变成名词，如 fixation 与 isolation。

abstract.en: Sequestration is a locked room with a neutral keyholder.
abstract.cn: sequestration 是一间上锁的屋子，钥匙在一位中立方手里。

abstract.en: It is the paperwork of separation.
abstract.cn: 它是分离的文书形式。

abstract.en: Every sense asks the same question: who holds it, and for how long.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在问同一个问题：谁保管它，保管多久。

examples.en: The judge ordered the sequestration of the disputed funds.
examples.cn: 法官下令扣押争议资金。

examples.en: Sequestration of the jury is rare because it is expensive and disruptive.
examples.cn: 陪审团隔离很少使用，因为代价高且扰乱生活。

examples.en: The word sequestration now appears most often in carbon policy.
examples.cn: sequestration 如今最常出现在碳政策中。

dict_mnemonic.text: sequestration（另行保管）＝把东西分开、交给中立方看管；同一动作依次落到财产、陪审团、预算、死骨、金属与二氧化碳上。

root: 拉丁 sequestrare「另行放置、交付保管」，源自 sequester「受托人、中间人」；更早来源不确定，一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one move: separation plus custody. They run from the general act through jury, property, budget, lung, chemistry, carbon, church income and figurative isolation.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享一个动作：分开加保管。从一般行为依次经过陪审团、财产、预算、肺、化学、碳、教会收入，到比喻性的隔绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a disputed object is locked in a third party's cabinet, and the key is held by neither claimant.
core.cn: 核心意象：有争议的物品被锁进第三方的柜子，钥匙不在任何一方当事人手里。

branches.en: THE CORE AND ITS FIGURE: setting aside in general, then the plain-language image of being cut off.
branches.cn: 核心与比喻：先是一般的另行放置，再是日常语言里的隔绝意象。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PROPERTY: the jury held away from news, the assets held by a third party.
branches.cn: 人与财物：陪审团被隔在新闻之外，资产由第三方保管。

branches.en: THE TREASURY: funds withheld by rule when limits are breached.
branches.cn: 国库：上限被突破时按规则扣下的资金。

branches.en: BODY AND MOLECULE: tissue cut off from the airway, an ion locked into a complex.
branches.cn: 身体与分子：与气道隔开的组织，被锁进络合物的离子。

branches.en: GAS AND CHURCH: carbon put under guard, income held for a vacant benefice.
branches.cn: 气体与教会：被看管起来的碳，为空缺教职代管的收入。

intro.en: Sequestration is a Latin legal noun with a productive family in law, medicine and climate policy.
intro.cn: sequestration 是一个拉丁法律名词，在法律、医学与气候政策中都有能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sequester, sequestrare and sequestrum; there is no separate prefix to parse, since the whole word came through as one unit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 sequester、sequestrare 与 sequestrum；这里没有可拆的前缀，因为整个词是作为一个单位传入的。

items.example: Sequester is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sequester 是整个词族的词基。

items.meaning: to set aside; to give into custody
items.exampleCN: sequestrare 产生了这个英语名词。

items.example: The Latin noun of action became English sequestration.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动作名词变成英语 sequestration。

items.meaning: the act or state of being set apart
items.meaningCN: 被分开保管的行为或状态
items.example: The word carries a legal tone in every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在每个义项里都带着法律语气。

items.meaning: to take legal custody of property
items.exampleCN: 法院在判决前扣押资产。

items.example: The sequestrated estate could not be sold.
items.exampleCN: 被扣押的产业不能出售。

items.meaning: a piece of dead bone separated from living tissue
items.meaningCN: 与活组织分离的死骨片
items.example: Surgeons remove a sequestrum to cure infection.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生切除死骨片以治愈感染。

items.meaning: surgical removal of a dead bone fragment
items.example: Sequestrotomy is a rare procedure today.
items.exampleCN: 死骨切除术如今很少施行。

definition_zh: 自大的；傲慢鲁莽的；自负冒失的
definition_en: offensively self-assertive and conceited
core_image: 拍着胸脯夸海口的小人物
scene: 新来的助理对老员工指手画脚，人人皱眉。 His bumptious manner annoyed the whole office.
sceneCN: 这里 bumptious 是「自大傲慢的、冒失的」（第 1 个义项：自以为是且爱逞能）；句意是他傲慢的做派惹恼了全办公室。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「傲慢自大地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「自大，傲慢」
近义词，义为「放肆的，自以为是的」

senses.title: Conceited and pushy
senses.definition: obnoxiously self-confident and forward in dealing with others
senses.definitionCN: 过分自信，待人接物咄咄逼人
senses.example: The bumptious intern corrected the director twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个不知天高地厚的实习生两次纠正主管。
senses.why: The root bump suggests one who butts in and bumps others aside.
senses.whyCN: 词根 bump 暗示那种横冲直撞、把旁人挤开的做派。

senses.title: Loudly self-assertive in manner
senses.definition: making one's importance loudly and plainly felt
senses.definitionCN: 大张旗鼓地显摆自身的重要
senses.example: His bumptious speech earned only embarrassed silence.
senses.exampleCN: 他趾高气扬的演讲只换来尴尬的沉默。
senses.why: Pushiness that fails reads as noisy vanity.
senses.whyCN: 逞能而不奏效，便只剩下聒噪的虚荣。

senses.title: Cheeky toward superiors
senses.definition: disrespectfully forward toward those of higher rank or age
senses.definitionCN: 对长辈或上位者轻慢放肆、不知进退
senses.example: The sergeant rebuked the bumptious recruit.
senses.exampleCN: 中士训斥了那个放肆的新兵。
senses.why: Self-assertion aimed upward crosses into insolence.
senses.whyCN: 自我张扬一旦指向尊者，便逾越为冒犯。

intro.en: Bumptious is a nineteenth-century English coinage, probably blending bump with a -tious ending.
intro.cn: bumptious 是十九世纪的英语造词，一般认为是 bump 与 -tious 词尾的混合。

items.en: bump echoes a blunt knock or shove.
items.cn: bump 摹仿莽撞的推挤之声。

items.en: the older phrase bumptious for bounteous may have fed the blend.
items.cn: 旧义 bumptious（= bounteous，慷慨）或为该混成词提供了词尾。

items.en: writers coined the modern sense of pushy self-conceit.
items.cn: 十九世纪作家赋予其「逞强自负」的新义。

items.en: novelists used it for officious minor characters.
items.cn: 小说家常以之刻画好管闲事的小人物。

items.en: bumptious remains a literary word for pompous pushiness.
items.cn: 如今 bumptious 仍是书面语，形容倨傲逞强。

note.en: Bumptious rhymes with -tious adjectives and stands among the arrogance words.
note.cn: bumptious 与 -tious 结尾的形容词押韵，置身「傲慢」词群之中。

entries.definition: in a bumptious way
entries.definitionCN: bumptious 的副词形式

entries.definition: the quality of being bumptious
entries.definitionCN: 自大，bumptious 的名词形式

entries.definition: going beyond proper limits
entries.definitionCN: 放肆的，拼写相近且意义相邻，但词根不同

entries.definition: generous; the older sense of bumptious
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨的，bumptious 的旧义同源说法

entries.definition: overly proud and self-important
entries.definitionCN: 傲慢的，自大的

entries.definition: aggressively self-assertive
entries.definitionCN: 咄咄逼人的，爱出风头的

entries.definition: self-important in a solemn way
entries.definitionCN: 自命不凡的，浮夸的

entries.definition: annoyingly noticeable or forward
entries.definitionCN: 冒失扎眼的

entries.definition: rudely disrespectful
entries.definitionCN: 无礼放肆的

normalIntro.en: He bumps into every conversation, certain he belongs at the front.
normalIntro.cn: 他横冲直撞地插进每个话题，认定自己理当前排。

normal.en: Feel the bump inside the word: a pusher, a shover.
normal.cn: 感受词中的 bump：一个爱挤爱撞的人。

normal.en: -tious makes adjectives like loquacious and audacious.
normal.cn: -tious 构形容词，如 loquacious、audacious。

normal.en: Older dictionaries once listed bumptious as bounteous.
normal.cn: 旧词典曾把 bumptious 当作 bounteous 的变体。

normal.en: The word is literary, common in nineteenth-century novels.
normal.cn: 该词偏书面，多见于十九世纪小说。

normal.en: Pushy is the everyday cousin of bumptious.
normal.cn: pushy 是 bumptious 的口语近亲。

abstract.en: See a small man swell like a frog to look taller.
abstract.cn: 看见小个子鼓成青蛙，只求显得高大。

abstract.en: Hear his voice two levels louder than the room.
abstract.cn: 听他的嗓门高出全场两个档次。

abstract.en: Feel elbows nudging you aside at the front desk.
abstract.cn: 感受前台的胳膊肘把你往外挤。

examples.en: The critic dismissed the memoir as bumptious self-praise.
examples.cn: 评论家讥这本回忆录尽是自大的自夸。

examples.en: Even as a boy he was bumptious, correcting his teachers.
examples.cn: 他打小便不知分寸，动辄纠正老师。

examples.en: Her bumptious confidence masked deep insecurity.
examples.cn: 她张扬的自信底下藏着深深的不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蹦身死」——自大的人爱蹦跶显摆，蹦到人前「身」败名裂才肯罢休。

root: bumptious 一般认为是十九世纪的英语混成词：取 bump（撞、挤）配 -tious 形容词词尾而成，或受旧义 bumptious（= bounteous，慷慨）影响；词源结构说法不一，无古典拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: A pusher who bumps others aside reads first as conceited, then as showy, and finally as insolent toward rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 把旁人挤开的莽撞者，先被读作自负，继而张扬，最终对尊长放肆无礼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a self-important man shoving to the front of the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：自命不凡者硬挤到队伍最前。

branches.en: a bumptious new manager
branches.cn: 自大的新经理

branches.en: bumptious boasting at the party

branches.en: a bumptious public speech
branches.cn: 张扬浮夸的公开演讲

branches.en: a bumptious reply to the colonel

definition_zh: 通风的；宽敞明亮的；轻快的；不切实际的
definition_en: full of fresh air, light and spacious, cheerful and light in manner, or lacking substance
core_image: 开满窗的白色房间：风穿过，光线也穿过，什么都留不住
scene: 她推开门，海风一下子灌满了整个房间。 The studio has an airy loft with tall windows on every side.
sceneCN: 这里 airy 是「通风的、宽敞明亮的」（第 1 个义项：空气流通、光线充足）；句意是工作室的阁楼四面高窗，明亮通透。

pos.zh: 通风的；明亮的；轻快的；空洞的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「空气；神态」；airy 由其加 -y 构成

airy 加 -ness，义为「通风；轻盈；空洞」

senses.title: Full of fresh air and light
senses.definition: having plenty of fresh air moving through, and feeling open and light
senses.definitionCN: 空气流通、光线充足，令人感觉开阔轻盈
senses.example: The kitchen is airy, with windows on two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房两面开窗，通风明亮。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns air into a quality; a room with air moving through it is literally 'full of air'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把 air 变成一种性质；空气流通的房间就是字面上的「满是空气」。

senses.title: Cheerful and casual in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a light, easy, and unconcerned way
senses.definitionCN: 举止轻松随意、若无其事
senses.example: She gave an airy wave and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻快地挥了挥手，继续往前走。
senses.why: Air is weightless, so a person acting 'like air' moves lightly and lets nothing weigh on them.
senses.whyCN: 空气没有重量，举止「像空气一样」的人便步履轻盈、百事不萦怀。

senses.title: Lacking substance or detail
senses.definition: not based on facts or solid plans; vague and unrealistic
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏事实或切实计划支撑的；含糊而不现实的
senses.example: The candidate offered airy promises instead of a plan.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人只给了空洞的承诺，拿不出方案。
senses.why: What is made of air has no weight and cannot be held, so airy ideas are ones you cannot grasp.
senses.whyCN: 空气做的东西没有分量也抓不住，因此 airy 的想法就是无法落实的想法。

intro.en: A simple English compound: the noun air plus the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: 简单的英语复合词：名词 air 加形容词后缀 -y。

items.en: aer meant the lower air, the layer human beings breathe.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指低层大气，即人呼吸的空气。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aer, keeping the sense of air and atmosphere.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 aer，仍指空气、大气。

items.en: Old French air passed the word on to English with its Greek-Latin pedigree intact.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词连同希腊-拉丁血统一并传给英语。

items.en: air entered English in the sense of the atmosphere we breathe.
items.cn: 14 世纪 air 进入英语，指我们呼吸的大气。

items.en: airy was formed with -y, first describing open, well-ventilated places.
items.cn: 16 世纪加 -y 构成 airy，最初形容开阔通风之处。

items.en: The word widened to light manners and empty, insubstantial ideas.
items.cn: 词义扩大到轻快的举止与空洞的想法。

note.en: The first group collects look-alikes of airy; the second collects words for open spaces and empty words.
note.cn: 第一组收与 airy 形近的词；第二组收「开阔」与「空洞」两义的近义词。

entries.definition: informal British word for impractical and vague ideas
entries.definitionCN: （英式口语）空想的；不切实际的

entries.definition: a literary variant of airy, also meaning an eagle's nest
entries.definitionCN: airy 的文学变体，亦指鹰巢

entries.definition: strange and frightening; only pronounced similarly, different root
entries.definitionCN: 诡异吓人的；仅与 airy 音近，词源不同

entries.definition: in a light, casual, or unconcerned way
entries.definitionCN: 轻快地；漫不经心地

entries.definition: large and with plenty of room inside
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞的；空间大的

entries.definition: with a light wind, or cheerful and relaxed
entries.definitionCN: 有微风的；轻松愉快的

entries.definition: not clear or precise, like airy promises
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的；不明确的

entries.definition: extremely light and delicate, seeming not of this world
entries.definitionCN: 轻盈飘渺的；超凡的

entries.definition: empty inside, as of hollow words
entries.definitionCN: 空心的；（话语）空洞的

normalIntro.en: The word is air plus -y: full of air, and so light.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 air 加 -y：满是空气，所以轻盈。

normal.en: An airy room lets the wind walk through it.
normal.cn: 通风的房间能让风穿堂而过。

normal.en: An airy wave is a light, careless little movement.
normal.cn: airy wave 是轻描淡写的小动作。

normal.en: Airy promises are made of air: nothing to hold.
normal.cn: 空洞的承诺是空气做的：抓不住任何东西。

normal.en: airy-fairy is the informal cousin for unrealistic ideas.
normal.cn: airy-fairy 是它的口语近亲，形容不切实际。

normal.en: airily is the adverb: she replied airily.
normal.cn: airily 是副词：她轻快地答道。

abstract.en: Picture curtains lifting in a tall white room.
abstract.cn: 想象高大的白房间里窗帘被风掀起。

abstract.en: See a girl waving as she drifts past, feet barely touching the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个女孩飘然而过，脚尖几乎不沾地。

abstract.en: Imagine grabbing at a soap bubble and finding your hand full of nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象去抓肥皂泡，摊开手却什么都没有。

examples.en: They chose the apartment for its airy rooms.
examples.cn: 他们选中这套公寓是因为房间明亮通风。

examples.en: He waved an airy hand and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他随意地摆了摆手，转换了话题。

examples.en: The plan was dismissed as airy nonsense.
examples.cn: 这个计划被斥为空洞的空想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿瑞」——爱儿住的房子通风又亮堂，心里舒坦得很。

root: 名词 air 源自希腊语 aer「低层大气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；16 世纪加形容词后缀 -y 构成 airy，由「通风」引申出「轻快」与「空洞」二义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses follow air itself: rooms full of it, manners as light as it, and ideas with nothing in them.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都跟着 air 走：满是空气的房间，像空气一样轻的举止，以及空无一物的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open window in a white room, wind and light passing through, nothing held back.
core.cn: 核心意象：白屋敞窗，风与光穿堂而过，无一物滞留。

branches.en: tall windows pulling a breeze through a studio
branches.cn: 高窗把微风引进画室

branches.en: a light wave of the hand, feet barely on the ground
branches.cn: 轻描淡写的挥手，脚尖几乎不着地

branches.en: a speech full of promises and empty of plans
branches.cn: 满是承诺、空无方案的演讲

branches.en: the weightless manner and the weightless idea behind it
branches.cn: 没有分量的举止，与举止背后没有分量的想法

branches.en: one quality of air, filling rooms, gestures, and words
branches.cn: 空气的同一性质，充盈着房间、姿态与言辞

intro.en: A Greek-Latin noun for air plus the common English adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: 希腊-拉丁语源的名词 air，加常见英语形容词后缀 -y。

latinIntro.en: aer is the recorded Latin borrowing from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: aer 是有记录的拉丁语对希腊语的借用。

items.meaning: of the air, existing in the air

definition_zh: 社会融合；社会整合：不同群体、个体与制度在日常往来中被纳入同一个社会整体，并形成稳定联系的过程与状态
definition_en: the process or state in which different groups, individuals and institutions are brought into one society and held together by stable everyday ties
core_image: 一条老街区的新旧住户在同一张长桌上分食，孩子在桌下交换玩具，界线在日常往来里一点点消失
scene: 社区中心把新迁来的家庭与老住户请到同一张长桌，孩子先在桌下交换玩具，大人们随后谈起共同的学校问题。 Social integration grows through small daily contacts rather than through a single official ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里指不同群体在日常往来中被纳入同一社会整体的过程（第 1 个义项：群体层面的社会融合）；句意为社会融合靠日常的小接触累积，而不是靠一场官方仪式。

pos.zh: 社会融合（不可数，指群体被纳入整体的过程）
社会整合（社会学用语，指社会各部分被联结的状态）

forms.label: 形容词性短语（已融入社会的）
核心名词的名词化形式

derivatives.zh: integrate + -ion（动作或结果）→ 整合这一过程或其结果
integrate + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 具有整合作用的
integration + -ist（主张者）→ 主张社会融合的人或立场
dis-（相反） + integrate → 由「使完整」反转为「使解体」
re-（重新） + integrate → 重新纳入整体，语义偏移为「回归社会」
social + -ly（方式副词）→ 以社会交往的方式

senses.title: Groups drawn into everyday contact
senses.titleCN: 不同群体在日常往来中被纳入同一整体
senses.definition: the process by which newcomers and established residents come to share ordinary daily contacts, schools and workplaces
senses.definitionCN: 新来者与原住户逐渐共享日常接触、学校与工作场所的过程
senses.example: Evening language classes became the cheapest route to social integration.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间语言课成了社会融合最省钱的途径。
senses.why: the phrase joins social, from Latin socius 'companion', with integration, from integrare 'to make whole', so it literally names the making of companions out of strangers.
senses.whyCN: 短语由表示「同伴」的 social 与表示「使完整」的 integration 组成，字面上说的就是把陌生人变成同伴。

senses.title: The sociological concept of cohesion
senses.titleCN: 社会学意义上的社会凝聚力
senses.definition: the degree to which members of a society feel bound by shared norms and collective life, as treated in classical sociology
senses.definitionCN: 社会成员受共同规范与集体生活约束的程度，是古典社会学的研究对象
senses.example: Durkheim treated social integration as a buffer against anomic suicide.
senses.exampleCN: 涂尔干把社会整合视为抵御失范性自杀的缓冲。
senses.why: sociology took the everyday phrase and gave it a collective, measurable reading: how tightly are members held together?
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这个日常短语收为集体的、可测量的概念，追问成员被联结得有多紧。

senses.title: Coordination among institutions
senses.titleCN: 机构之间的协调与整合
senses.definition: the fitting together of separate institutions, such as schools, health services and labour offices, into one working system
senses.definitionCN: 把学校、卫生服务、劳动部门等分立机构装进一个运转系统
senses.example: Social integration of the health and housing services cut waiting time for new arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生与住房服务的整合缩短了新来者的等待时间。
senses.why: integration also names the fitting of parts into a whole, so the phrase extends from people to the institutions that serve them.
senses.whyCN: integration 也指把各部分装进整体，于是短语从人延伸到服务于人的机构。

senses.title: Inclusion of pupils in mainstream schools
senses.titleCN: 学生被纳入普通学校与普通班级
senses.definition: the placement and participation of pupils with disabilities or minority backgrounds in ordinary classrooms
senses.definitionCN: 让残障或少数群体背景的学生进入普通课堂并真正参与
senses.example: The district measured social integration by how often pupils with aides joined group work.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区用有陪读的学生参加小组活动的频率来衡量社会融合。
senses.why: school is the first place where a society's parts meet daily, so the phrase naturally names classroom inclusion.
senses.whyCN: 学校是社会各部分每天相遇的第一现场，因此短语自然用来指课堂接纳。

senses.title: Entry into the labour market
senses.titleCN: 进入劳动力市场并获得工作网络
senses.definition: the movement of migrants or excluded groups into paid work, training and the networks that form at work
senses.definitionCN: 移民或被排斥群体进入有薪工作、培训以及工作中形成的关系网络
senses.example: Apprenticeships did more for social integration than leaflets about equality.
senses.exampleCN: 学徒制对社会融合的作用，比平等主题的宣传单更大。
senses.why: a job puts people into repeated contact under shared rules, which is exactly the mechanism the phrase describes.
senses.whyCN: 工作把人放进共享规则下的反复接触，这正是短语所描述的机制。

senses.title: Shared urban space and mixed neighbourhoods
senses.titleCN: 共享城市空间与混合居住的街区
senses.definition: the condition in which different income and ethnic groups use the same streets, parks and public services
senses.definitionCN: 不同收入与族裔群体使用同样的街道、公园与公共服务
senses.example: Planners argued that mixed housing would promote social integration more than a new community centre.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者认为混合住房比新建社区中心更能促进社会融合。
senses.why: integration needs a physical surface, and shared space is where strangers become familiar.
senses.whyCN: 融合需要一个物理表面，共享空间正是陌生人变得熟悉的地方。

senses.title: Participation in online communities
senses.titleCN: 在线上社群中获得参与与承认
senses.definition: the process by which isolated or new users become recognised participants in an online group
senses.definitionCN: 孤立或新来的用户成为线上群体中被承认的参与者
senses.example: Moderators used welcome threads to support social integration of shy newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 版主用欢迎帖帮助羞怯的新成员融入社群。
senses.why: contact, recognition and shared rules reappear wherever a group meets, including on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 接触、被承认与共享规则的同一模式会出现在任何群体相遇之处，屏幕上也不例外。

senses.title: A measured level of union
senses.definition: a quantified degree to which groups are linked, used as a variable in surveys and policy evaluation
senses.definitionCN: 群体被联结的程度被量化为指标，用于调查与政策评估
senses.example: The survey scored social integration from zero to ten and compared regions.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查用零到十分给社会融合打分，并比较各地区。
senses.why: once the process is understood it can be scored, and the phrase then names the score rather than the process.
senses.whyCN: 过程一旦被理解就可以打分，短语于是指那个分数，而不是过程本身。

intro.en: The phrase joins two Latin-derived nouns. Social goes back to Latin socius 'companion, ally'; integration goes back to integer 'whole, untouched' and integrare 'to make whole'. The phrase itself is a modern sociological formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源的名词组成。social 追溯至拉丁 socius「同伴、同盟」；integration 追溯至 integer「完整、未受触动」与 integrare「使完整」。短语本身是近代社会学的构造。年代为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, associate'. Standard references connect it with sequi 'to follow', so a companion is one who follows or accompanies; socialis in Late Latin meant 'of companions, of alliance'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、同盟、伙伴」。通行词源资料把它与 sequi「跟随」联系起来，同伴即同行之人；晚期拉丁 socialis 意为「同伴的、结盟的」。

items.en: Integer 'whole, complete, untouched' is built from in- 'not' and the root tag- 'to touch' seen in tangere. The same root gives intact and contact.
items.cn: integer「完整、未受触动」由 in-「不」与 tangere 中可见的 tag-「触碰」词根构成。同一词根还给出 intact 与 contact。

items.en: Integrare meant 'to make whole, to renew, to restore'. Its noun integratio named a renewal or a restoring of a whole, first in religious and later in general prose.
items.cn: integrare 意为「使完整、更新、恢复」。其名词 integratio 指更新或使整体复原，先用于宗教文字，后进入一般散文。

items.en: Social entered English through Old French social, and integration through French integration in the eighteenth century, both keeping the Latin sense of joining or making whole.
items.cn: social 经古法语进入英语，integration 在 18 世纪经法语 integration 进入，两者都保留拉丁语「联结、使完整」的意思。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the two words were combined in sociology, above all in Durkheim's work, to name the binding of individuals and groups into a collective life.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪末起，两个词在社会学中被组合使用，尤其在涂尔干的著作里，用来指个体与群体被联结为集体生活。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation of the exact phrase): the combination formed gradually in sociological writing, so no single first use is established; the link of socius to sequi and the pre-Latin origin of the root are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切短语的首见书证）：这一组合在社会学写作中逐步形成，没有公认的首次使用；socius 与 sequi 的联系及其拉丁语之前的来源均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds expressions that look close in form but name something else; group two holds near neighbours that describe related but distinct social processes.
note.cn: 第一组是形式相近却指别的事的表达；第二组是语义相邻、但描述不同社会过程的词。

entries.definition: The process by which a child or newcomer learns the norms and skills of a society; it names learning, not the resulting union of groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指儿童或新来者学习社会规范与技能的过程，强调的是学习，而非群体最终形成的联结。

entries.definition: A policy phrase about giving excluded people access to services and opportunities; it stresses access rather than the ties that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 关于让被排斥者获得服务与机会的政策短语，强调「能够进入」，而非随后形成的联结。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of society as a whole'; it describes a level of analysis and never names a process of joining.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「整个社会的」，只描述分析层次，从不指联合的过程。

entries.definition: The process by which a minority group is absorbed into the dominant culture, often at the cost of its own language; integration does not demand that cost.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体被主流文化吸收的过程，往往以其自身语言为代价；社会融合不要求这种代价。

entries.definition: The strength of the bonds that hold a society together; it names the resulting glue, while integration names the movement that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 把社会维系在一起的联结强度，指作为结果的黏合力，而 integration 指产生它的运动。

entries.definition: The practice of admitting people to opportunities and settings; it covers access, whereas integration also covers the ties formed after access.
entries.definitionCN: 把人接纳进机会与场所的做法，覆盖「进入」；integration 还覆盖进入之后形成的联结。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: socialis 'of companions' plus integrare 'to make whole': making companions out of strangers.
normal.cn: socialis「同伴的」加 integrare「使完整」：把陌生人做成同伴。

normal.en: Integer is 'untouched, whole', built from in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'.
normal.cn: integer 是「未受触动、完整」，由 in-「不」加 tangere「触碰」的词根构成。

normal.en: The family runs social, society, sociable, integrate, integral, integrity, integration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 social、society、sociable、integrate、integral、integrity、integration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the public sense: promote social integration, barriers to social integration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出公共义：促进社会融合、社会融合的障碍。

normal.en: Its opposite in policy talk is segregation, the separating of groups that integration would join.
normal.cn: 政策话语中的反义是 segregation，即把本应联合的群体分开。

abstract.en: Picture two tables pushed together until the seam is too narrow to see.
abstract.cn: 想象两张桌子被推到接缝窄得看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a torn map rejoined, with the crease still faintly visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一张撕开的地图被重新拼合，折痕仍隐约可见。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that joins two villages yet belongs to neither of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥把两个村子连起来，却不属于任何一村。

examples.en: The city funded evening classes as a tool of social integration.
examples.cn: 该市资助夜间课程，把它作为社会融合的工具。

examples.en: High-rise estates can slow social integration when they isolate newcomers.
examples.cn: 高层住宅区若把新来者隔离开，会拖慢社会融合。

examples.en: Surveys that measure social integration must distinguish contact from trust.
examples.cn: 测量社会融合的调查必须把接触与信任区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: social（社会的）+ integration（整合）＝ 社会整合；记「陌生人先在长桌旁同坐，再在同一套规则里同住」。

root: 拉丁 socius「同伴、同盟」（通行词源资料与 sequi「跟随」相联系）+ 拉丁 integer「完整、未受触动」＝ in-「不」+ tangere「触碰」，经 integrare「使完整」；短语在 19 世纪末社会学文献中逐步定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: strangers meet, meet again under shared rules, are counted as members, and finally the meeting itself is turned into a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个运动展开：陌生人相遇、在共享规则下反复相遇、被算作成员，最后连这场相遇本身也被折算成分数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two groups around one long table, with the boundary between them fading as ordinary contact repeats.
core.cn: 核心意象：两组人围在同一张长桌旁，随着日常接触反复发生，他们之间的界线逐渐消失。

branches.en: DAILY CONTACT: the phrase begins with ordinary encounters between newcomers and established residents.
branches.cn: 日常接触：短语从新来者与原住户的普通相遇开始。

branches.en: TIE AND FITTED PARTS: sociology measures the collective bond, while institutions are the parts being fitted into one system.
branches.cn: 联结与装配：社会学测量集体的黏合，机构则是被装进同一系统的部件。

branches.en: TWO DOORS: the classroom and the workplace are where repeated contact turns into membership.
branches.cn: 两扇门：课堂与职场是反复接触转变为成员身份的地方。

branches.en: TWO SURFACES: shared streets and shared screens give the same process a place to happen.
branches.cn: 两个表面：共享的街道与共享的屏幕给同一过程提供发生之处。

branches.en: THE SCORE: what was a process becomes a number that policy can compare across regions.
branches.cn: 分数：原本是过程的东西变成一个可在地区间比较的数字。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are Latin nouns built from a root and a suffix, and both roots also build large English families, so the phrase can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 短语的两半都是词根加后缀构成的拉丁名词，两个词根还各构成一个英语大词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis supply the social half; integer, integrare and integratio supply the integration half. The prefix in- in integer is negative, not the in- of 'into'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 socialis 提供 social 这一半；integer、integrare 与 integratio 提供 integration 这一半。integer 中的 in- 是否定前缀，不是表示「进入」的 in-。

items.example: The root names the person one travels with.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指与自己同行的人。

items.example: The adjective moved the root from persons to relations.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把词根从人转向关系。

items.example: The abstract noun names the whole formed by companions.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指同伴们形成的整体。

items.example: What is not touched remains whole.
items.exampleCN: 未被触碰的东西保持完整。

items.example: Its root supplies intact and contact as well.
items.exampleCN: 它的词根还给出 intact 与 contact。

items.example: The verb turns wholeness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「完整」变成动作。

items.example: The action suffix names the process rather than the actor.
items.exampleCN: 动作后缀命名的是过程，而不是施动者。

items.structure: social (English adjective, from Old French social)
items.example: The adjective describes the human side of the union.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述联结中属于人的一面。

items.meaning: the act or result of making whole
items.example: The noun names both the work and its outcome.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指工作，也指结果。

items.example: The suffix marks a person who takes a side.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记采取某一立场的人。

latinEntries.structure: integer, integra, integrum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 听得见的；可闻的
definition_en: able to be heard; loud or clear enough to reach the ear
core_image: 声音越过距离传到耳朵里：能被听见
scene: 后排的家长踮起脚，仍听不清台上的致辞。 The speaker's voice was barely audible over the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 audible 指「听得见的」（第 1 个义项：声音可被听到）；句意：演讲者的声音在风里几乎听不见。

derivatives.zh: 听得见地；出声地（audible + -ly）
可闻度；能听清的程度（audible + -ity）
听不见的（in- 否定前缀 + audible）
听众；观众（同族词，出自 audire「听」）
音频的；声音的（同族词）

senses.title: Loud enough to hear
senses.definition: loud or clear enough to be heard
senses.definitionCN: 响亮或清晰到足以被听见的
senses.example: Her voice was barely audible at the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 在礼堂后排几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: The root audire means to hear; -able marks what can undergo it.
senses.whyCN: 词根 audire 意为「听」；-able 标记「可被……的」。

senses.title: Within human hearing range
senses.definition: of sound waves, within the range humans can perceive
senses.definitionCN: （声波）处于人耳可感知范围内的
senses.example: Dogs hear frequencies well beyond the audible range.
senses.exampleCN: 狗能听到远超人耳听域的频率。
senses.why: Physics fixed the word to a measured band: too high or too low is inaudible.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个词锚定在一段可测的频带：过高过低都不可闻。

senses.title: Expressed out loud
senses.definition: of a feeling, made audible as a sound, such as a sigh or groan
senses.definitionCN: （情绪）以叹息、呻吟等声音形式发出来的
senses.example: She gave an audible sigh of relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她如释重负，发出一声听得见的叹息。
senses.why: Silent feelings become audible the moment they escape as sound.
senses.whyCN: 无声的情绪一旦化作声音逸出，便成为「可闻」的。

senses.title: Clearly heard by listeners
senses.definition: of speech or broadcast sound, clear enough for an audience
senses.definitionCN: （讲话、广播声音）对听众足够清晰的
senses.example: Check that every speaker is audible from the last row.
senses.exampleCN: 确认每位发言人的声音在最后一排都能听清。
senses.why: In public speaking the test is the farthest ear, so the word measures reach.
senses.whyCN: 公开演讲的检验标准是最远的那只耳朵，这个词便成了「传到与否」的量尺。

senses.title: Perceptible in recordings
senses.definition: of a sound in a recording, present and distinguishable on playback
senses.definitionCN: （录音中的声音）回放时存在且可分辨的
senses.example: A second voice is faintly audible in the background of the tape.
senses.exampleCN: 磁带背景里隐约能听到第二个声音。
senses.why: Recordings create a second ear, and audible now marks what survives onto it.
senses.whyCN: 录音创造了第二只耳朵，audible 如今标记能在这只耳朵上留痕的声音。

senses.title: Detectable by instruments of hearing
senses.definition: of a signal, present in the audio channel or detectable as sound
senses.definitionCN: （信号）存在于音频通道或可作为声音检出的
senses.example: An audible warning sounds when the door is not closed.
senses.exampleCN: 车门未关好时会响起声音警报。
senses.why: Engineering needs an adjective for signals the ear can catch, and this one fits.
senses.whyCN: 工程上需要一个形容词来指耳朵能捕捉的信号，这个词正合适。

senses.title: Easily heard, emphasized
senses.definition: used with negatives or adverbs to grade how well a sound carries
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词或副词连用，为声音的传达程度分等
senses.example: His whisper was just audible over the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨声中他的低语勉强可闻。
senses.why: Hearing is a gradient, so the word lives with barely, faintly, and just.
senses.whyCN: 听觉本是个渐变量，这个词便常与 barely、faintly、just 为伴。

senses.title: In sports, a called play
senses.titleCN: （美式橄榄球）临场喊出的战术
senses.definition: in American football, an audible is a play called at the line of scrimmage
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中指在开阵线前临场改喊的战术
senses.example: The quarterback called an audible seconds before the snap.
senses.exampleCN: 开球前几秒，四分卫临场改喊了战术。
senses.why: A play that exists only as a shouted word is literally made of hearing.
senses.whyCN: 只存在于一声喊叫里的战术，名副其实地由「听」构成。

intro.en: Audible comes from Latin audibilis, formed on audire, to hear; English borrowed it from the Latin past participle stem audit- plus -ibilis in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: audible 出自拉丁语 audibilis，其基础是动词 audire「听」；15 世纪英语从拉丁语过去分词词干 audit- 加 -ibilis 将其借入。

items.en: The root *h₂ewis- meant to perceive, to hear, feeding the Latin hearing family.
items.cn: 词根 *h₂ewis- 意为「感知、听见」，孕育了拉丁语「听」的词族。

items.en: audire meant to hear; its participle stem audit- and adjective audibilis meant able to be heard.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audire 意为「听」；其分词词干 audit- 与形容词 audibilis 意为「可被听见的」。

items.en: audibilis joined the verb stem with -ibilis, the standard Latin ending for able to be.
items.cn: audibilis 由动词词干加 -ibilis 构成，后者是拉丁语表示「可……的」的标准词尾。

items.en: audible entered English in the fifteenth century, first in learned and religious texts.
items.cn: audible 于 15 世纪进入英语，最初见于学术与宗教文本。

items.en: Science and music widened its use to measured ranges of sound.
items.cn: 科学与音乐把它扩展到可测量的声音范围。

items.en: From radio engineering to football play-calling, audible now marks every sound that reaches an ear or channel.
items.cn: 从无线电工程到橄榄球战术口令，audible 如今标记一切能抵达耳朵或声道的信号。

note.en: Group one collects the hear-family and the aud- look-alikes from the dare root; group two collects neighboring hearing words.
note.cn: 第一组收「听」词族及与「敢」词根同以 aud- 开头的形近词；第二组收相邻的听觉词。

entries.definition: a group of listeners, from Latin audientia, a hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 听众；观众，出自拉丁语 audientia「听」。

entries.definition: the hall where people listen, literally the hearing place.
entries.definitionCN: 礼堂；听众席，本义即「听的地方」。

entries.definition: bold, from Latin audax, to dare; shares only the aud- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的，出自拉丁语 audax「敢」；仅拼写同以 aud- 开头。

entries.definition: relating to the sense of hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；与听觉相关的。

entries.definition: clearly heard or seen, easily told apart.
entries.definitionCN: 清晰的；容易分辨的。

entries.definition: able to be noticed by any sense, hearing included.
entries.definitionCN: 可感知的；不限听觉。

entries.definition: deep, full, and resonant in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 浑厚响亮的；低沉有回响的。

entries.definition: too faint or high or low to be heard.
entries.definitionCN: 听不见的；audible 的反义词。

entries.definition: of the ear and hearing as a sense, not of a single sound.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉层面的；与单一声音相对。

normalIntro.en: audible wears its root on its sleeve: audi means hear, able means can.
normalIntro.cn: audible 把词根写在脸上：audi「听」+ able「能够」。

normal.en: audi + able: able to be heard, exactly as visible means able to be seen.
normal.cn: audi + able：能被听见，正如 visible 是能被看见。

normal.en: The audi family: audience, auditorium, audio, audible, all about hearing.
normal.cn: audi 家族：audience、auditorium、audio、audible——都关于「听」。

normal.en: Add in- and the sound vanishes: inaudible.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 声音便消失：inaudible。

normal.en: barely audible is the everyday phrase for a voice that hardly carries.
normal.cn: barely audible 是形容声音几乎传不到的日常说法。

normal.en: In football an audible is a play you can only know by hearing it.
normal.cn: 橄榄球里的 audible 是只能靠听来领会的战术。

abstract.en: Picture a sound crossing a noisy square and still arriving at one ear.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音穿过嘈杂广场，仍抵达了一只耳朵。

abstract.en: Audible is the moment silence breaks.
abstract.cn: audible 是寂静被打破的那一刻。

abstract.en: Think of a volume knob: audible is anywhere above zero.
abstract.cn: 把它想成音量旋钮：零以上皆为 audible。

examples.en: The teacher's voice stayed audible even at the back of the playground.
examples.cn: 即使在操场尽头，老师的声音也清晰可闻。

examples.en: There was an audible gasp when the results appeared on the screen.
examples.cn: 结果出现在屏幕上时，全场响起清晰的倒吸气声。

examples.en: The recording was old, but every word remained audible.
examples.cn: 录音年代久远，但每个字仍然听得清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥弟」——奥秘弟在外屋大声唱歌，隔着门也听得见

root: 出自拉丁语 audire「听」（过去分词词干 audit-）+ 形容词后缀 -ibilis「可……的」，即 audibilis「可被听见的」；15 世纪进入英语，与 audience、audio、auditorium 同属「听」词族，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hearing adjective: from sheer loudness through measured ranges and escaped sighs to the football call that lives only in sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随一个「听」的形容词：从纯粹的响度，到可测的频带、逸出的叹息，再到只存在于声音里的橄榄球战术口令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound that completes its journey to an ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：完成抵达耳朵之旅的声音。

branches.en: THE LOUDNESS SCALE: barely audible to clearly audible.
branches.cn: 响度标尺：从勉强可闻到清晰可闻。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SIDE: hearing ranges, warnings, and signals.
branches.cn: 可测一面：听域、警报与信号。

branches.en: ESCAPED SOUND: sighs and background voices on tape.
branches.cn: 逸出的声音：叹息与磁带里的背景人声。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE SIDE: speech that must reach the last row.
branches.cn: 听众一面：必须传到最后一排的讲话。

branches.en: THE FIELD SIDE: the football play called in a shout.
branches.cn: 赛场一面：一声喊出的橄榄球战术。

intro.en: audible is built transparently: the verb stem audi- plus -able, exactly parallel to visible and readable.
intro.cn: audible 结构一目了然：动词词干 audi- 加 -able，与 visible、readable 完全平行。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, to hear, anchors a wide family: audience, audio, auditory, auditorium, audition, and audible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听」统率一个庞大词族：audience、audio、auditory、auditorium、audition 与 audible。

definition_zh: n. 带扣；v. 扣紧；（因压力）弯曲变形，垮掉
definition_en: a metal fastener on a belt or strap; to fasten with one; also to bend or give way under pressure
core_image: 皮带扣在门口松开，只能弯腰重新扣好
scene: 皮带扣在门口松开了，他弯腰把它扣回去。 The buckle came loose at the door, and he bent to fasten it.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：buckle 指带扣；句意是皮带扣在门口松开，他弯腰扣回去。

derivatives.zh: 圆盾
扣环；扣住
扣件

senses.title: A metal fastener
senses.definition: a metal frame with a pin, used to fasten a belt or strap
senses.definitionCN: 带别针的金属框，用来扣住皮带或带子
senses.example: The buckle on his bag had rusted.
senses.exampleCN: 他包上的扣子生了锈。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin buccula, a cheek piece of a helmet.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自拉丁语 buccula，指头盔的护颊片。

senses.title: To fasten with a buckle
senses.definition: to close or join something with a buckle
senses.definitionCN: 用带扣把东西扣上或连起来
senses.example: Buckle your seat belt before the car moves.
senses.exampleCN: 车开动前系好安全带。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 名词不变形就变成了动词。

senses.title: To bend or give way
senses.definition: to bend out of shape, or to stop resisting under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 变形成弯，或在压力下不再支撑
senses.example: The bridge buckled in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 桥在高温下变形了。
senses.why: A bent metal buckle is the image for a person giving way.
senses.whyCN: 被压弯的金属扣，就是人「撑不住」的意象。

intro.en: Buckle comes from Latin buccula, the cheek piece of a helmet.
intro.cn: buckle 来自拉丁语 buccula，指头盔的护颊片。

items.en: Buccula is a small cheek plate.
items.cn: buccula 是一小块护颊板。

items.en: Boucle means a boss or a buckle.
items.cn: boucle 意为凸饰或带扣。

items.en: English buckle names a belt fastener.
items.cn: 英语 buckle 指皮带扣。

items.en: To buckle is to fasten with one.
items.cn: to buckle 指用扣扣紧。

items.en: Buckles appear in engineering failure reports.
items.cn: 扣的结构进入工程失效报告。

items.en: Buckle under pressure is figurative.
items.cn: buckle under pressure 为比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the buck- start or the -kle ending; the near-meaning group covers fasteners and the act of giving way.
note.cn: 形近组共享 buck- 开头或 -kle 词尾；近义组兼收扣件与「撑不住」。

entries.definition: An open container for liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 盛液体的敞口容器。

entries.definition: A male deer, or a dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 公鹿；美元。

entries.definition: A joint of a finger.
entries.definitionCN: 指关节。

entries.definition: To laugh quietly.
entries.definitionCN: 低声笑。

entries.definition: A device that holds two parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两部分扣在一起的装置。

entries.definition: Anything that fastens.
entries.definitionCN: 任何固定用的东西。

entries.definition: A small device that grips.
entries.definitionCN: 夹住东西的小装置。

entries.definition: To stop resisting or supporting.
entries.definitionCN: 不再抵抗或支撑。

normalIntro.en: A buckle holds a belt together, and also names the moment a thing stops holding.
normalIntro.cn: buckle 既扣住皮带，也指某物「扣不住」的那一刻。

normal.en: Buckle is both a noun and a verb.
normal.cn: buckle 既是名词也是动词。

normal.en: As a noun it is a metal fastener.
normal.cn: 作名词是金属扣。

normal.en: As a verb it fastens, as in buckle up.
normal.cn: 作动词表示扣紧，如 buckle up。

normal.en: It also means to bend and give way.
normal.cn: 它还表示弯曲、撑不住。

normal.en: A belt that will not close is the image.
normal.cn: 扣不上的皮带就是那个意象。

abstract.en: Metal meeting metal and holding.
abstract.cn: 金属相扣而固定。

abstract.en: A strap pulled one hole tighter.
abstract.cn: 把带子收紧一格。

abstract.en: A body losing its shape under weight.
abstract.cn: 身体在重量下失去形状。

examples.en: He buckled the strap of his helmet.
examples.cn: 他扣好头盔的带子。

examples.en: Please buckle up before we leave.
examples.cn: 出发前请系好安全带。

examples.en: The metal frame buckled under the weight.
examples.cn: 金属框架在重压下变形了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 原指头盔护颊的小金属片，后来成为「皮带扣」。

root: 拉丁语 buccula（护颊小片）

sensesIntro.en: A buckle is a small piece of metal whose whole purpose is to decide whether two things stay joined.
sensesIntro.cn: buckle 是一小片金属，它的全部职责就是决定两样东西是否继续连在一起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a belt buckle coming loose at a doorway
core.cn: 核心意象：门口松开的皮带扣

branches.en: A rusted buckle on an old bag.
branches.cn: 旧包上生锈的扣子。

branches.en: A seat belt clicked shut.
branches.cn: 咔哒扣上的安全带。

branches.en: A bridge bending in heat.
branches.cn: 高温下变形的桥。

branches.en: A team giving way under pressure.
branches.cn: 压力下垮掉的团队。

branches.en: Holding, then failing to hold.
branches.cn: 先扣住，后扣不住。

intro.en: Buckle is a French borrowing; the list below covers it and the vocabulary of fastening.
intro.cn: buckle 是法语借词；下面列出它以及「扣紧」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin bucca is a cheek, and figere is to fix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bucca 意为脸颊，figere 意为固定。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bucca 产生 buckle 与 buccal。
figere 产生 fix 与 prefix。
firmus 产生 firm 与 confirm。

definition_zh: 附加；添加；追加（尤其在文件末尾）
definition_en: to add something to the end of a written document or piece of writing
core_image: 挂在末尾：像在长卷末尾续接一张纸
scene: 报告写完后，秘书在最后又贴上了一页附录。 She decided to append a detailed table to the end of her report.
sceneCN: 这里 append 是「在文末附加」（第 1 个义项：把内容加到末尾）；句意为：她决定在报告末尾附加一张详表。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词后缀构成，义为「附录；阑尾」
同根派生，义为「附加物；附属肢体」
加形容词后缀 -ant，义为「附加的；附加物」
appendix 加炎症后缀，义为「阑尾炎」

senses.title: To add to the end of a text
senses.definition: to add writing or material at the end of a document
senses.definitionCN: 在文件末尾添加文字或材料
senses.example: The lawyer appended two exhibits to the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在合同后附上两份证物。
senses.why: The root pendere means to hang, so the basic image is hanging something at the tail of a text.
senses.whyCN: 词根 pendere 意为悬挂，基本意象就是把东西挂在一篇文章的尾部。

senses.title: To add data in computing
senses.definition: to add data to the end of an existing file, string, or list
senses.definitionCN: 把数据加到已有文件、字符串或列表的末尾
senses.example: The program appends each log entry to a file.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把每条日志追加到文件里。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the paper image: new bytes hang at the tail of the old file.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域借用了纸面意象：新字节挂在旧文件的尾部。

senses.title: To attach as a supplement
senses.definition: to attach something secondary that supports the main text
senses.definitionCN: 附上支撑正文的次要材料
senses.example: She appended her research notes for reference.
senses.exampleCN: 她附上研究笔记供参考。
senses.why: What hangs at the end is usually support material, giving the supplement sense.
senses.whyCN: 挂在末尾的通常是辅助材料，于是产生补充义。

senses.title: To affix a signature or seal
senses.definition: to add one's signature or seal to a document
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上加署签名或盖章
senses.example: He appended his signature without reading the terms.
senses.exampleCN: 他没看条款就签了字。
senses.why: A signature hangs at the bottom of a page, an image of physical attachment.
senses.whyCN: 签名悬在页底，是物理附着的意象。

senses.title: To add conditions or clauses
senses.definition: to add extra conditions, clauses, or requirements
senses.definitionCN: 追加额外的条件、条款或要求
senses.example: They appended several conditions to the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在协议上附加了几个条件。
senses.why: Conditions ride at the tail of the main deal, extending the end-attachment image.
senses.whyCN: 条件挂在主交易后面，延伸了末尾附着的意象。

senses.title: To continue a record
senses.definition: to extend an ongoing record by adding new entries
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加新条目延续进行中的记录
senses.example: The captain appended the day's events to the logbook.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把当天的事件续记进航海日志。
senses.why: Records grow by hanging new lines after old ones.
senses.whyCN: 记录靠在旧行后面挂上新行来生长。

senses.title: To add as a lesser attachment
senses.definition: to add something regarded as secondary or less important
senses.definitionCN: 加上被视为次要或不太重要的东西
senses.example: Critics felt the ending was merely appended.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者觉得结尾只是硬接上去的。
senses.why: Because the tail is secondary to the body, appended can imply low status.
senses.whyCN: 尾巴相对身体是次要的，appended 因此可暗示地位低。

senses.title: To string together in sequence
senses.definition: to join pieces one after another into a single sequence
senses.definitionCN: 把片段一个接一个连成单一序列
senses.example: The editor appended the chapters into one volume.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把各章串接成一册。
senses.why: Repeated hanging builds a chain, giving the sequence sense.
senses.whyCN: 反复悬挂连成一串，于是产生序列义。

intro.en: Append comes from Latin appendere, to hang something onto something else, from ad- plus pendere.
intro.cn: append 来自拉丁语 appendere（把某物悬挂在另一物上），由 ad- 加 pendere 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *(s)pen- meant to draw, stretch, or spin.
items.cn: 重构词根 *(s)pen- 意为拉、伸、纺。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang or weigh; with ad- it formed appendere, to hang upon.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂、称重；加 ad- 构成 appendere，意为悬挂其上。

items.en: Appendere developed the sense of paying or attaching as a dependency.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中 appendere 发展出依附、归属之义。

items.en: English took append directly from Latin in the fifteenth century, first in legal use for dependencies.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪直接从拉丁语借入 append，最初用于法律语境表附属。

items.en: It now chiefly means to add material to the end of a text or file.
items.cn: 如今它主要指在文本或文件末尾添加材料。

note.en: Append belongs to a large pend-family and sits beside several add-words.
note.cn: append 属于庞大的 pend 词族，并与若干「添加」类词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 书末附录；阑尾

entries.definition: a part attached to a larger body
entries.definitionCN: 附加物；附属肢体

entries.definition: to hang something up or stop it temporarily
entries.definitionCN: 悬挂；暂停

entries.definition: to fasten or join one thing to another

entries.definition: to put something together with something else

entries.definition: to add or join territory or a building
entries.definitionCN: 兼并；附加（领土、建筑）

normalIntro.en: The pend-family of hanging words unlocks append instantly.
normalIntro.cn: 「悬挂」词族 pend 一族能让你秒懂 append。

normal.en: append = ap- (toward) + pend (hang): hang it onto the end.
normal.cn: append = ap-（朝向）+ pend（悬挂）：挂到末尾。

normal.en: Same root as appendix, the thing appended at the back of a book.
normal.cn: 与 appendix 同根，即书末被附加的部分。

normal.en: Same family: suspend, depend, pendant — all about hanging.
normal.cn: 同族词：suspend、depend、pendant——都关乎悬挂。

normal.en: In programming, append means adding to the end of a list or file.
normal.cn: 在编程里，append 表示加到列表或文件末尾。

normal.en: Opposite idea: prepend adds to the front instead.
normal.cn: 对比记：prepend 是加到开头。

abstract.en: Picture clipping one more page to the tail of a long scroll.
abstract.cn: 想象在长卷末端再夹上一页纸。

abstract.en: A charm hangs at the end of a bracelet — appended, not inserted.
abstract.cn: 手链末端挂着坠子——是附加而非插入。

abstract.en: Append sounds like 'a pen': use a pen to add the last line.
abstract.cn: append 听着像 a pen：用笔补上最后一行。

examples.en: Please append your initials to each page.
examples.cn: 请在每一页附上你的姓名首字母。

examples.en: The report appended a glossary of technical terms.
examples.cn: 报告在后面附上了术语表。

examples.en: You can append new records without rewriting the file.
examples.cn: 你可以在不重写文件的情况下追加新记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿盆的」——把文件扔进「阿盆」的末尾再添一勺，谐音只助记，不是词源。

root: 拉丁词根 pend-/pens-（悬挂、称重）：append 由 ad-（朝向）+ pendere（悬挂）构成，本义「悬挂于上」，引申为「把材料挂在文末」，即附加。

sensesIntro.en: From hanging material at the tail of a text, append spreads to file data, supplements, signatures, conditions, records, subordinate attachments, and sequenced strings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把材料挂在文末」出发，append 依次铺开到文件数据、补充材料、签名、附加条件、记录续接、次要附属与按序串接。

core.cn: 核心意象：把东西悬挂在一篇文字的尾部

branches.en: physical marks of attachment: texts, signatures, conditions
branches.cn: 物理附着痕迹：文本、签名、条件

branches.en: growing records: file data and ongoing logs
branches.cn: 生长的记录：文件数据与进行中的日志

branches.en: support material that completes the main text

branches.en: subordinate status of what hangs at the tail
branches.cn: 挂在尾部的次要地位

branches.en: strings of pieces joined in sequence
branches.cn: 按序串接的片段

intro.en: Append is a clean compound of a prefix and the pend root, the source of dozens of English words.
intro.cn: append 由前缀加 pend 词根干净地拼成，这一词根是几十个英语词的来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang or weigh, is one of the most fruitful roots in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称重）是英语里最高产的词根之一。
