definition_zh: 添加剂；添加物；附加的；加法的
definition_en: a substance added to something in small amounts, or an adjective meaning added or relating to addition
core_image: 一小勺粉末倒进面糊，颜色立刻变了
scene: 厨房里，面点师往面粉中倒进一小袋白色粉末，面团很快变得松软。 The label lists every additive used in the bread.
sceneCN: 这里 additive 是「添加剂」（第 1 个义项：少量加入以改变性质的东西）；句意为标签列出了面包中使用的每一种添加剂。

derivatives.zh: 本词对应的动词，义为「加；添加」
由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「加法；添加」
由 addition 加 -al 构成，义为「附加的；额外的」

senses.title: A food additive
senses.definition: a substance added to food in small amounts to preserve it, colour it or improve its texture
senses.definitionCN: 为防腐、着色或改善质地而少量加入食物中的物质
senses.example: The label warns that the drink contains several additives.
senses.exampleCN: 标签提示这种饮料含有多种添加剂。
senses.why: Addere means to give to, and -itive marks a thing that is added, so a food additive is literally a giving-into the recipe.
senses.whyCN: addere 意为「给到」，-itive 标记「被加入之物」，所以食品添加剂字面上就是「加进配方里的东西」。

senses.title: A fuel or oil additive
senses.definition: a chemical added to fuel or lubricant to improve performance or protect the engine
senses.definitionCN: 加入燃油或润滑油以改善性能或保护发动机的化学物质
senses.example: The mechanic recommended a cleaning additive for the old engine.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工建议给旧发动机加一种清洁添加剂。
senses.why: The same structure appears in machines: a small added substance changes how the main fluid behaves.
senses.whyCN: 同样的结构出现在机器里：少量加入的物质改变了主要液体的表现。

senses.title: Additive manufacturing
senses.definition: a production method that builds objects layer by layer instead of cutting material away
senses.definitionCN: 逐层堆积材料而非切削去除材料的制造方法
senses.example: Additive manufacturing made the custom part in a single day.
senses.exampleCN: 增材制造在一天之内就做出了这个定制零件。
senses.why: Material is added layer upon layer, so the adjective describes the direction of the build rather than a chemical ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 材料一层一层被加上去，所以这个形容词描述建造的方向，而不是化学配料。

senses.title: Additive colour
senses.definition: colour produced by mixing light, where added colours make the result brighter
senses.definitionCN: 通过混合光产生的颜色，加入颜色会使结果更亮
senses.example: Screens use additive colour, mixing red, green and blue light.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕使用加色，把红、绿、蓝光混合起来。
senses.why: Light adds to light, unlike paint, so the adjective marks a mixing system that increases brightness.
senses.whyCN: 光加到光上，与颜料不同，所以这个形容词标记一种会增加亮度的混合系统。

senses.title: An additive effect
senses.definition: a combined effect equal to the simple sum of separate effects
senses.definitionCN: 等于各单独效应简单相加之和的合并效应
senses.example: The two drugs have an additive effect on blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种药物对血压有叠加效应。
senses.why: If effects simply add, one plus one stays two, which is the mathematical meaning of the word applied to causes.
senses.whyCN: 如果效应只是相加，一加一仍等于二，这就是这个词的数学含义被用到原因上。

senses.title: Additive identity and inverse
senses.titleCN: 加法单位元与加法逆元
senses.definition: in mathematics, the number zero that leaves a sum unchanged, or the number that cancels another
senses.definitionCN: 数学中使总和不变的零，或使另一个数被抵消的数
senses.example: Zero is the additive identity because adding it changes nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 零是加法单位元，因为加上它不改变任何东西。
senses.why: These terms describe the rules of addition itself, so the adjective names a role inside the operation.
senses.whyCN: 这些术语描述加法本身的规则，所以这个形容词命名的是运算中的一种角色。

senses.title: Added as an extra
senses.definition: describing something added on top of what already exists, often as an extra charge or feature
senses.definitionCN: 形容在现有事物之上追加的东西，常指额外收费或额外功能
senses.example: The additive charge appears on a separate line of the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 附加费用出现在账单的单独一行。
senses.why: The adjective can simply describe anything extra, keeping the plain sense of something given in addition.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可以单纯描述任何额外之物，保留「额外加上」的朴素含义。

senses.title: An additive statistical model
senses.definition: a model in which the total value is the sum of separate components
senses.definitionCN: 总量等于各独立成分之和的模型
senses.example: The additive model assumes that each factor contributes independently.
senses.exampleCN: 加性模型假定每个因素独立地作出贡献。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the arithmetic sense to say that parts combine only by adding, with no interaction.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用算术含义，表示各部分只通过相加结合，没有交互作用。

intro.en: Additive is the adjective and noun form of the Latin verb addere, to give to; English built it with -ive.
intro.cn: additive 是拉丁动词 addere「给到」的形容词与名词形式；英语用 -ive 构成。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it also lies behind data and donate.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，也藏在 data 与 donate 背后。

items.en: Ad plus dare formed addere, to give to or add; its participle additus means added.
items.cn: ad 与 dare 构成 addere「给到、添加」，其分词 additus 意为「被添加的」。

items.en: Late Latin additivus meant pertaining to adding; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 additivus 意为「与添加有关的」，确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: The English adjective appears in scientific writing, first in mathematics and chemistry.
items.cn: 英语形容词先出现在科学写作中，最早用于数学与化学。

items.en: As industrial food and fuel grew, the noun additive became common for substances added in small amounts.
items.cn: 随着工业食品与燃料发展，名词 additive 常指少量加入的物质。

items.en: Additive manufacturing extended the word to a method of building objects layer by layer.
items.cn: additive manufacturing 把这个词扩展到逐层堆积物体的制造方法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers add-family words; the near-meaning group gathers substances and descriptors of extra things.
note.cn: 形近组收 add 词族；近义组收添加物与描述额外之物的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adding or the thing added.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加的行为」或「被添加之物」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put something in addition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加、添加」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra or supplementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、补充的」。

entries.definition: A thing added at the end of a text; a different noun from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补遗」，指文末追加之物，是同一动词的另一名词形式。

entries.definition: A number added to another; a precise cousin of additive in arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加数」，是 additive 在算术中的近亲。

entries.definition: One of the substances that make up a mixture; a normal component rather than a small extra.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成分、配料」，是混合物的正常组成部分，而非少量额外添加物。

entries.definition: A specific kind of additive that prevents food from spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「防腐剂」，是添加剂中专门防止食物变质的一类。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete, often a nutrient or extra dose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充剂、补充物」，指为改善或补全而添加的东西。

entries.definition: An additional item beyond what is usual; broader and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「额外的」，范围更宽、技术性更弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real addere root and the food, fuel and manufacturing phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 addere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的食品、燃料与制造搭配。

normal.en: Additive is the thing given into a mixture, from addere, to give to.
normal.cn: additive 是被加进混合物里的东西，来自 addere「给到」。

normal.en: A food additive is listed on the label because it was added in small amounts.
normal.cn: 食品添加剂会列在标签上，因为它是少量加入的。

normal.en: Additive manufacturing adds layers; subtractive manufacturing removes material.
normal.cn: additive manufacturing 是增加层，subtractive manufacturing 则是去除材料。

normal.en: Additive colour mixes light, so more colour means more brightness.
normal.cn: additive colour 混合的是光，所以颜色越多亮度越高。

normal.en: An additive effect is exactly the sum of the separate effects.
normal.cn: additive effect 正好等于各单独效应之和。

abstract.en: Picture a small spoon of white powder falling into a bowl of dough and changing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一小勺白色粉末落进一碗面团，把面团改变了。

abstract.en: The word is about small amounts with large effects: a little added, a lot changed.
abstract.cn: 这个词讲的是少量却有大效果：加了一点，变了很多。

abstract.en: Additive is the opposite of taking away; it builds by putting something on.
abstract.cn: additive 与「拿掉」相反；它靠往上加东西来建造。

examples.en: The bakery removed all artificial additives from its bread.
examples.cn: 这家面包店从面包中去掉了所有人工添加剂。

examples.en: Additive manufacturing can produce shapes that traditional cutting cannot.
examples.cn: 增材制造能做出传统切削做不到的形状。

examples.en: The additive effect of the two treatments was stronger than either alone.
examples.cn: 两种疗法的叠加效应比单独使用任何一种都强。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe something added: a food or fuel substance, a layer-wise production method, a light-mixing system, a summed effect, a mathematical role, an extra charge, or a statistical assumption.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「被加入之物」：食品或燃料物质、逐层制造方法、混光系统、相加效应、数学角色、额外收费，或统计假设。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small spoon of powder falls into dough and changes its texture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小勺粉末落进面团，改变了它的质地。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: food and fuel receive a small chemical that changes behaviour.
branches.cn: 物质线：食品与燃料接受少量改变其表现的化学物质。

branches.en: THE METHOD: layers or light are added rather than removed.
branches.cn: 方法线：增加的是层或光，而不是被去除。

branches.en: THE SUM: effects or model components combine by simple addition.
branches.cn: 总和线：效应或模型成分通过简单相加结合。

branches.en: THE RULE: mathematics names roles inside the operation.
branches.cn: 规则线：数学为运算内部的各种角色命名。

branches.en: THE EXTRA: the plain sense of something added on top.
branches.cn: 额外线：某物被追加在上面的朴素含义。

intro.cn: additive 是拉丁分词词干加英语形容词后缀；名词用法从形容词生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare, addere and additivus are recorded; the English form follows the Latin adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare、addere、additivus 均有记录；英语形式沿用拉丁形容词。

definition_zh: 行为生态学：研究动物行为如何被生态环境塑造、又如何反过来影响生存与繁殖的分支学科
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies how ecological conditions shape animal behavior and how that behavior in turn affects survival and reproduction
core_image: 一只鸟在食物稀少的年份把觅食范围画得很大，在丰收年份又缩回巢边，地图上的圈随年景一张一缩
scene: 同一种鸟在食物稀少的年份扩大觅食范围，在食物充足时缩短，研究者据此统计每种策略留下的后代数量。 The team counts how many offspring each strategy yields and asks why the bird widens its search only when food is scarce, a standard question in behavioral ecology.
sceneCN: 这里 behavioral ecology 指「研究行为与生态环境相互作用的学科」（第 1 个义项：作为学科名）；句意为研究者统计不同觅食策略留下的后代数量，并追问鸟为何只在食物稀少时扩大搜索范围，这是行为生态学的典型问题。可辨识物件：逐年变化的觅食圈、巢、幼鸟、记录表。

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为一门学科的行为生态学
senses.definition: the subfield of biology that joins the study of behavior to the study of ecological conditions
senses.definitionCN: 把行为研究与生态条件研究结合起来的生物学分支
senses.example: Behavioral ecology grew rapidly after the 1960s.
senses.exampleCN: 行为生态学在 20 世纪 60 年代后迅速发展。
senses.why: The compound names exactly what it joins: one half supplies the conduct, the other the environment in which that conduct must pay off.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词精确命名了它所连接的两半：一半提供行为，另一半提供行为必须在此获得回报的环境。

senses.title: The central question of adaptive value
senses.titleCN: 核心问题：行为的适应价值
senses.definition: the question of how a behavior raises or lowers an animal's chances of surviving and reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 某种行为如何提高或降低动物存活与繁殖机会的问题
senses.example: The paper asks the central behavioral ecology question: what does the display cost, and what does it buy?
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文提出行为生态学的核心问题：这种展示付出什么代价，又换回什么。
senses.why: Ecology supplies the currency, survival and offspring; behavior is then judged by what it earns in that currency.
senses.whyCN: 生态学提供货币，即存活与后代；行为则按它在这种货币中赚到什么来评判。

senses.title: A research programme treating behavior as a trait
senses.titleCN: 把行为当作性状的研究纲领
senses.definition: an approach that treats a behavior as a biological trait shaped by selection, like a beak or a wing
senses.definitionCN: 把某种行为当作受选择塑造的生物性状，如同喙或翅膀
senses.example: Treating nest defense as a trait changed how the team designed its experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 把护巢当作一种性状，改变了研究组设计实验的方式。
senses.why: If a behavior can be inherited and selected, it can be measured like any other trait, which is the move that made the field possible.
senses.whyCN: 既然行为可以遗传并被选择，它就能像别的性状一样被测量，正是这一步使这门学科成为可能。

senses.title: Analysis of behavioral strategies
senses.definition: the comparison of alternative strategies an animal might adopt under given conditions
senses.definitionCN: 对动物在给定条件下可能采取的各种替代策略的比较
senses.example: The model compares two foraging strategies under the same rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型比较同一降雨条件下的两种觅食策略。
senses.why: Once behavior is a trait, variants of it can be lined up as options, and the field asks which option pays best where.
senses.whyCN: 一旦行为成为性状，它的各种变体就能排成选项，这门学科便追问在何处哪个选项回报最高。

senses.title: Interface with population ecology
senses.definition: the study of how individual behavior changes birth rates, death rates and population size
senses.definitionCN: 个体行为如何改变出生率、死亡率与种群规模的研究
senses.example: Territory size links behavioral ecology to population ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 领地大小把行为生态学与种群生态学连接起来。
senses.why: When many individuals behave in the same way, their choices add up to births and deaths, so the field borders population ecology.
senses.whyCN: 当许多个体以同样方式行动，其选择就累加成出生与死亡，这门学科因此与种群生态学接壤。

senses.title: Interface with evolutionary biology
senses.definition: the study of how behavior evolves and how evolutionary history constrains it
senses.definitionCN: 行为如何进化、进化历史又如何限制行为的研究
senses.example: Comparative work places the dance of one species beside that of its relatives.
senses.exampleCN: 比较研究把某一物种的舞蹈与近缘物种的舞蹈并置。
senses.why: A trait that pays off is inherited, so the field must ask about ancestry as well as about present conditions.
senses.whyCN: 能带来回报的性状会被继承，因此这门学科既要问当下的条件，也要问祖先的来源。

senses.title: Application in conservation
senses.titleCN: 在保护生物学中的应用
senses.definition: the use of behavioral findings to plan reserves, reintroductions and wildlife management
senses.definitionCN: 用行为研究的发现来规划保护区、再引入与野生动物管理
senses.example: Behavioral ecology guided where the corridor was placed.
senses.exampleCN: 行为生态学指导了廊道的选址。
senses.why: If animals avoid a gap or refuse a new site, the map of a reserve must include their conduct, not only the habitat's area.
senses.whyCN: 如果动物回避某处空隙或拒绝新地点，保护区的图就必须纳入它们的举止，而不只是栖息地面积。

senses.title: Abstract: any behavior-environment analysis
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何「行为—环境」互动分析
senses.definition: any framework that reads conduct as an answer to environmental conditions, even outside biology
senses.definitionCN: 任何把举止读作对环境条件的回答的框架，即便在生物学之外
senses.example: The author applies behavioral ecology to how shoppers move through a market.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把行为生态学用于分析顾客如何在市场里移动。
senses.why: At its widest the compound becomes a template: any agent whose choices are shaped by scarce resources can be read this way.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个复合词成了一个模板：任何选择受稀缺资源塑造的主体都能这样解读。

intro.en: Behavioral ecology joins an English noun to a Greek-derived one. Behavior is native, from behave; ecology was coined in the nineteenth century from Greek oikos 'house, household' plus -logia 'study'.
intro.cn: behavioral ecology 把一个英语名词与一个希腊来源的名词结合起来。behavior 属本族语，来自 behave；ecology 是 19 世纪用希腊 oikos「家、居所」加 -logia「研究」造出的词。

items.en: Behavior dates from the late fifteenth century, from behave, literally 'to carry oneself'. It supplies the conduct half of the compound.
items.cn: behavior 自 15 世纪晚期出现，来自 behave，字面为「把握自己」，为复合词提供「行为」这一半。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household, dwelling place', the root of economy as well as of ecology.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家户、居所」，既是 economy 也是 ecology 的词根。

items.en: Ernst Haeckel coined German Oekologie in 1866 from oikos plus -logia, and English ecology followed in the same decade.
items.cn: 恩斯特·海克尔于 1866 年用 oikos 加 -logia 造出德语 Oekologie，英语 ecology 在同一十年随之出现。

items.en: The compound behavioral ecology is generally dated to the mid-twentieth century, when the two fields were deliberately joined.
items.cn: behavioral ecology 这一复合词一般认为形成于 20 世纪中叶，当时这两个领域被有意地连接起来。

items.en: Journals and societies bearing the name appeared later in the century, fixing the compound as a discipline rather than a phrase.
items.cn: 以该名命名的期刊与学会在该世纪后段出现，使这个复合词固定为一门学科，而不再只是一个短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single earliest citation for the English compound is settled, and the exact first coining of the term is debated, so the century rather than a year is reliable.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个英语复合词的最早书证并无统一说法，术语最初由谁造出也有争论，因此可靠的只是世纪，而非具体年份。

note.en: Group one separates the parts and near-names of the compound; group two holds neighbouring disciplines that answer different questions about the same animals.
note.cn: 第一组区分这个复合词的组成部分与近似名称；第二组是邻近学科，对同样的动物回答不同的问题。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of behavior'; it names one half of the compound and cannot stand for the discipline by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「行为的」的形容词；它只命名复合词的一半，不能单独代表这门学科。

entries.definition: The study of organisms and their surroundings; joined to behavioral, it names the hybrid field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与其环境；与 behavioral 结合，才命名这门交叉学科。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior from Greek ēthos 'character'; it overlaps in subject but not in name or emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ēthos「性格」的动物行为研究；研究对象重叠，但名称与侧重不同。

entries.definition: The study of the biological basis of social behavior, closer to evolution than to ecology in its questions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会行为的生物学基础，其问题更靠近进化而非生态。

entries.definition: The study of how ecological conditions shape evolutionary change; behavioral ecology focuses on conduct within that frame.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生态条件如何塑造进化变化；行为生态学则在该框架内聚焦举止。

entries.definition: The study of births, deaths and numbers in a population; behavior enters it only through aggregated individual choices.
entries.definitionCN: 研究种群中的出生、死亡与数量；行为只能通过个体选择的累加进入其中。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior through controlled experiments and cross-species comparison, often indoors.
entries.definitionCN: 通过受控实验与跨物种比较研究动物行为，常在室内进行。

entries.definition: The school that explains behavior by stimulus and response; it is a method, not an ecological field.
entries.definitionCN: 以刺激—反应解释行为的学派；它是一套方法，而非生态学领域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: behavioral + ecology: conduct read against environment, two halves of one name.
normal.cn: behavioral + ecology：把举止放到环境里读，一个名字的两半。

normal.en: The family runs behavior, behavioral, ecology, behavioral ecologist, behavioural ecology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 behavior、behavioral、ecology、behavioral ecologist、behavioural ecology。

normal.en: Typical phrases: a question in behavioral ecology, behavioral ecology model, the rise of behavioral ecology.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：行为生态学中的一个问题、行为生态学模型、行为生态学的兴起。

normal.en: The Greek oikos 'house' in ecology is the same root as in economy.
normal.cn: ecology 中的希腊 oikos「家」与 economy 同根。

normal.en: The central currency is fitness: survival plus offspring.
normal.cn: 核心货币是适合度：存活加后代。

abstract.en: Picture a bird's search circle breathing in and out with the size of the harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟的觅食圈随收成大小一呼一吸。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every display is entered as cost on one side and offspring on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每次展示一边记代价，一边记后代。

abstract.en: Picture a market where the same behaviour is read as a response to scarcity.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，同样的举止被读作对稀缺的回应。

examples.en: Behavioral ecology explains the timing of migration as a response to food and risk.
examples.cn: 行为生态学把迁徙的时机解释为对食物与风险的反应。

examples.en: Her thesis sits at the border of behavioral ecology and population ecology.
examples.cn: 她的论文位于行为生态学与种群生态学的交界处。

examples.en: The course introduces behavioral ecology through a single breeding colony.
examples.cn: 这门课通过一个繁殖群体介绍行为生态学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「behavior（行为）+ ecology（生态）」——把行为放进环境里算账，看它换来多少生存与后代 → 行为生态学

root: behavior（本族语，be- + have）+ ecology（希腊 oikos「家」+ -logia「研究」，1866 年由海克尔造出）构成的学术复合词；无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the name of a discipline, through its central question and method, to its interfaces with neighbouring fields, its applications, and finally a general template for reading conduct against conditions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科名称出发，经其核心问题与方法，走到与邻近领域的交界、实际应用，最后落到把举止放到条件里读的一般模板。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a behavior plotted on the same map as the resources that make it pay.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一种行为画在与它收益相关的资源同一张地图上。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS QUESTION: a name, then the single question of what a behavior costs and earns.
branches.cn: 领域与问题：先是一个名字，再是行为付出什么、换回什么这唯一问题。

branches.en: MAKING BEHAVIOR MEASURABLE: treated as a trait, then lined up as alternative strategies.
branches.cn: 使行为可测量：先当作性状，再排成替代策略。

branches.en: TWO NEIGHBOURS: individual choices add up into populations, and inherited traits point back to ancestry.
branches.cn: 两个邻居：个体选择累加成种群，可继承的性状又指向祖先。

branches.en: APPLIED EDGE: conduct enters the map of a reserve.
branches.cn: 应用边缘：举止进入保护区的地图。

branches.en: GENERAL TEMPLATE: any agent whose choices answer scarcity.
branches.cn: 一般模板：任何其选择在回应稀缺的主体。

intro.en: The compound is built from two transparent pieces, each with its own history: a native English noun and a Greek-derived scientific term.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个透明的部分组成，每部分各有自己的历史：一个本族英语名词与一个希腊来源的科学术语。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: behavior is Germanic, and ecology is coined from Greek oikos and -logia. Latin supplied only the connective adjective suffix -al.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：behavior 属日耳曼语，ecology 由希腊 oikos 与 -logia 造出。拉丁语只提供了连接用的形容词后缀 -al。

definition_zh: v. 当心，谨防（常用于警示）；提防某人或某物
definition_en: to be careful of something dangerous; used especially in warnings

sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：beware 用于提醒人提防危险；句意是栅栏上的木牌提醒路人当心那条狗。

senses.title: To be on guard against danger
senses.definition: to be careful because something may be dangerous or harmful
senses.definitionCN: 因某物可能危险有害而小心
senses.example: Beware of the edge; the path crumbles there.
senses.exampleCN: 当心那处边缘，小路在那里塌了。
senses.why: Beware began as be ware, two words meaning be watchful.
senses.whyCN: beware 起初写作 be ware，两个词，意为「保持警觉」。

senses.title: To be cautious about a person
senses.definition: to treat a person with suspicion because they may deceive you
senses.definitionCN: 因对方可能欺骗而对其保持戒心
senses.example: Beware of anyone who offers a deal too good to be true.
senses.exampleCN: 要提防那些开出好得不像真的条件的人。
senses.why: The same watchfulness turns from a cliff edge to a human character.
senses.whyCN: 同一份警觉，从悬崖边转向人的品性。

intro.en: Beware was once two words, be ware, an order to stay watchful like a sentry.
intro.cn: beware 原本是两个词 be ware，是一句像哨兵口令般的「保持警觉」。

items.en: Old English waer means watchful and cautious.
items.cn: 古英语 waer 意为警觉、谨慎。

items.en: Beon is the verb to be, here used as a command.
items.cn: beon 是动词「是」，此处作命令式。

items.en: The phrase be ware is spoken as a warning to look out.
items.cn: 短语 be ware 作为「留神」的警告使用。

items.en: The two words merge into a single verb.
items.cn: 两个词合并成一个动词。

items.en: The word settles into notices such as beware of the dog.
items.cn: 这个词固定出现在「当心恶犬」一类告示上。

items.en: Beware usually stands alone or takes of before its object.
items.cn: 现代用法中 beware 常单独使用，宾语前加 of。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps be- verbs; the near-meaning group layers the alarm from a quiet adjective to a shouted command.
note.cn: 形近组保留 be- 动词；近义组把警报从安静的形容词排到喊出的命令。

entries.definition: To confuse someone completely.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全迷惑。

entries.definition: To happen to someone, usually badly.
entries.definitionCN: （不幸）降临于某人。

entries.definition: To make someone seem small.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低某人。

entries.definition: To surround a place with an army.
entries.definitionCN: 以军队围困某地。

entries.definition: Careful because of possible danger.
entries.definitionCN: 因可能有危险而谨慎。

entries.definition: Avoiding risk by thinking ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 预先思量以避风险。

entries.definition: Watching and ready to react.
entries.definitionCN: 警觉并随时反应。

entries.definition: To watch over and protect something.
entries.definitionCN: 看守并保护某物。

normalIntro.en: Beware is simply be ware, be watchful, so the warning is built into the spelling.
normalIntro.cn: beware 就是 be ware，保持警觉，警告的意思直接写在拼写里。

normal.en: Split it: be ware, meaning be watchful.
normal.cn: 拆开看：be ware，意思是保持警觉。

normal.en: Ware is the same watchful root as wary.
normal.cn: ware 与 wary 同出「警觉」一词根。

normal.en: A sentry saying be ware is saying beware.
normal.cn: 哨兵喊 be ware，就是在喊 beware。

normal.en: Wooden signs all over the world say beware of the dog.
normal.cn: 全世界的木牌上都写着当心恶犬。

normal.en: Where there is a warning, the word is beware.
normal.cn: 哪里有警示，哪里就有 beware。

abstract.en: A hand held up before a step.
abstract.cn: 迈步之前举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Attention paid in advance of harm.
abstract.cn: 在伤害到来之前付出的注意。

abstract.en: The cheapest form of protection.
abstract.cn: 最廉价的防护。

examples.en: Beware of the dog, the gate does not latch.
examples.cn: 当心这条狗，大门关不严。

examples.en: Travellers were told to beware of pickpockets in the square.
examples.cn: 旅客被告知在广场上要当心扒手。

examples.en: Beware, the roads freeze early on this hill.
examples.cn: 当心，这座山的道路结冰很早。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「别忘」——出门前别忘了提醒自己一句：当心。

root: be（是，保持）+ ware（警觉的）→ 保持警觉，即当心

sensesIntro.en: One watchfulness covers two objects: a dangerous thing in front of you and a dangerous person beside you.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份警觉对准两类对象：眼前的危险之物，以及身边的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked wooden board nailed to a fence, with two words of warning on it
core.cn: 核心意象：钉在栅栏上的一块歪木牌，上面只有两个字：当心

branches.en: A cliff edge marked with a rope.
branches.cn: 用绳子圈出的悬崖边缘。

branches.en: A contract with a missing page.
branches.cn: 少了一页的合同。

branches.en: Care taken before anything happens.
branches.cn: 在任何事发生之前就付出的小心。

scene: 考古队员蹲在土层旁，指着更深的一层说那才是最早的。 The archaeologists traced the pottery style to its antecedent in a far older culture.
sceneCN: 这里 antecedent 是「先例、前身」（第 1 个义项：在先的事物）；句意为考古学家把这种陶器样式追溯到更古老文化中的前身。

derivatives.zh: 由同族动词加 -ence 构成，义为「居先；优先」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「先前；在前」

senses.title: A preceding thing or event
senses.definition: a thing, event, or condition that exists or happens before another and often helps cause it
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事物之前存在或发生、并常有助其成因的事物、事件或条件
senses.example: The treaty's antecedents go back to a handshake between two kings.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约的前身可以追溯到两位国王的一次握手。
senses.why: The Latin participle antecedens means 'going before', so the noun names whatever is walking ahead in the chain of events.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词 antecedens 意为「走在前面的」，名词便指事件链条上走在前面的那个东西。

senses.title: The noun a pronoun refers back to
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or phrase that a pronoun stands for or points back to
senses.definitionCN: 语法术语，指代词所代表或回指的名词或名词短语
senses.example: In the sentence about Anna, her antecedent is the name Anna itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在关于安娜的句子里，her 的先行词就是名字 Anna。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the same spatial picture: the pronoun follows the path the noun has already walked.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了同样的空间画面：代词沿着名词已经走过的路跟在后面。

senses.title: A person's background or origins
senses.definition: a person's earlier history, background, or record, especially as a way of judging them
senses.definitionCN: 一个人早先的历史、背景或记录，尤用于对其作出评价
senses.example: The committee asked about his antecedents before the appointment.
senses.exampleCN: 任命之前委员会询问了他的过往经历。
senses.why: A life is also a chain, and the events that antecede the present person are his record.
senses.whyCN: 人生也是一条链，先于此刻这个人的那些事件，就是他的履历。

senses.title: Coming before in time or order
senses.definition: coming earlier in time, order, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在时间、顺序或重要性上更早、更靠前
senses.example: Antecedent droughts had already weakened the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的旱情已经削弱了收成。
senses.why: The participle works as an adjective: the thing keeps its 'walking ahead' position even when it only describes another noun.
senses.whyCN: 分词可以作形容词：即便只用来修饰名词，那个「走在前面」的位置依然保留。

intro.en: Antecedent comes from the Latin present participle antecedens of antecedere 'to go before', built on ante 'before' plus cedere 'to go'.
intro.cn: antecedent 来自拉丁语 antecedere「走在前面」的现在分词 antecedens，其构成为 ante「在前」加 cedere「走」。

items.en: The root *ked- meant 'to go, to yield', shared with the English verb cede.
items.cn: 词根 *ked- 意为「走、让步」，与英语动词 cede 同源。

items.en: Ante 'before' and cedere 'to go' formed antecedere, 'to go before in time or rank'.
items.cn: ante「在前」与 cedere「走」合成 antecedere，意为「在时间或级别上居先」。

items.en: The present participle antecedens meant 'going before', and Latin used it both of events and of grammatical reference.
items.cn: 现在分词 antecedens 意为「走在前面的」，拉丁语已用它指先发的事件，也指语法上的先行成分。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in logic and grammar, soon also for causes and family history.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入该词，先用于逻辑与语法，很快也用于指原因与家世。

items.en: Modern usage favors the plural antecedents for causes or background, and the grammar term remains standard.
items.cn: 现代用法多用复数 antecedents 指前因或背景，语法术语沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-stem family; the near-meaning group gathers words for things that come first.
note.cn: 形近组收同词干家族；近义组收各种「在先之物」的说法。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to happen earlier, or to write an earlier date on a document.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「早于；把日期填早」，与 antecedent 同根。

entries.definition: An earlier decision that serves as an example; note the shorter vowel and different first vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「先例；判例」。注意拼写相近、且确为近亲，但重音与首元音不同。

entries.definition: One's line of forebears; only loosely related in form, and different in root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「祖先；世系」。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An earlier case used as a guide or justification for later ones.
entries.definitionCN: 指被后来者引用或效仿的先例，法律与惯例色彩强。

entries.definition: A person or thing that comes before and signals what follows.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「先驱；前兆」，强调预告后来者的身份。

entries.definition: A thing that comes before another of the same kind, often in a development chain.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「前身；先导」，多用于演化或发展链条。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the walking stem cede-, the grammar term, and the plural form most common in writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「走」的词干 cede-、语法术语，以及书面语最常用的复数形式。

normal.en: ante + ced + ent: the one that has gone before.
normal.cn: ante 加 ced 加 ent：先走过去的那个。

normal.en: Grammar: the pronoun follows its antecedent like a shadow.
normal.cn: 语法上：代词像影子一样跟着它的先行词。

normal.en: Historians write about the antecedents of wars, revolutions, and treaties.
normal.cn: 历史学家写战争、革命、条约的前因。

normal.en: Precedent is the legal cousin: an antecedent you can cite in court.
normal.cn: precedent 是法律上的表亲：能在法庭上引用的先例。

normal.en: The plural antecedents often means simply 'background'.
normal.cn: 复数 antecedents 常常就是「背景、出身」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture footprints on a path that the pronoun steps into one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象小路上的脚印，代词一个个踩着它们前行。

abstract.en: Picture tree rings: each ring antecedes and explains the next.
abstract.cn: 想象树的年轮：每一圈都在前一圈之后并解释着它。

abstract.en: Picture an old family album opened before the interview.
abstract.cn: 想象面试之前被翻开的老相册。

examples.en: Scholars debate the antecedents of the modern novel.
examples.cn: 学者们争论现代小说的源头。

examples.en: Make sure every pronoun has a clear antecedent.
examples.cn: 确保每个代词都有明确的先行词。

examples.en: Her distinguished antecedents helped her career.
examples.cn: 她显赫的家世帮助了她的事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安梯先等」——他安好梯子先等着，后面的人才爬，就是「在先的那个」

root: 拉丁语 antecedere（走在前面）的现在分词 antecedens → 英语 antecedent；词干 ced- 表「走」，前缀 ante- 表「在前」，核心意象是「走在前头、被后随者回指」。

sensesIntro.en: From the general 'thing before' the senses branch into grammar, personal history, and the adjective use.
sensesIntro.cn: 由泛指的「在先之物」分出语法、个人经历与形容词用法三个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one walking ahead, followed and referred back to
core.cn: 核心意象：走在前头、被后来者跟随并回指的那一个

branches.en: The cause line: earlier events become the antecedents of history.
branches.cn: 因果线：更早的事件成为历史的前因。

branches.en: The grammar line: the noun walks first, the pronoun follows its path.
branches.cn: 语法线：名词先走，代词沿着它的路径跟随。

branches.en: The biography line: the years before the present person form a record.
branches.cn: 履历线：先于此刻本人的岁月构成一份记录。

branches.en: Both senses need a follower: a later event, or a pronoun.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一个跟随者：后发的事件，或一个代词。

branches.en: The adjective keeps the participle's position word: coming before.
branches.cn: 形容词用法保留了分词的方位义：在前的。

intro.en: The word is the Latin participle antecedent- plus the English noun and adjective ending -t.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁分词词干 antecedent- 加上英语常用的名词/形容词词尾 -t 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb and the participle behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示这个英语词族背后的动词与分词。

items.exampleCN: 它为 antecedent 提供「在前」义。
它为 antecedent 提供「走」义。

items.meaning: one that is doing, or in a state
items.example: It forms antecedent from the stem.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 precede 与 precedent。

items.example: It forms precursor, a cousin word.

definition_zh: 与……相关；对……有意义（强调与眼前的问题有实质联系、能影响判断）
definition_en: to have a direct bearing on the matter being discussed or to be useful for deciding it
core_image: 评审桌上一叠卷宗，主席只把与眼前案子真正有关的那几份推到桌子中间
scene: 评审会上，主席把一叠卷宗摊在桌上，问哪几份与眼前的案子真正有关。 The committee asked which of the files could be relevant to the case before them.
sceneCN: 这里指材料与正在审理的案子有实质联系（第 1 个义项：与议题直接相关）；句意为委员会问这些文件里哪些可能与面前的案子有关。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成叠卷宗、被推到中间的那几份。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「相关性、切题」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「切题地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不相关的」
与本词同出拉丁语「抬起、减轻」一词，义为「减轻、缓解」
由同源动词的名词形进入英语，义为「缓解、宽慰」

senses.title: Bearing on the matter at hand
senses.definition: to have a direct connection with the question being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 指与被讨论的问题有直接联系
senses.example: Only the figures that can be relevant to the question should appear in the summary.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可能与问题有关的数字才应出现在摘要里。
senses.why: Relevance began in the courtroom, where a fact matters only if it bears on the case.
senses.whyCN: 「相关性」最早出自法庭，一项事实只有在与案件有关时才被算数。

senses.title: Useful for solving a problem
senses.titleCN: 对解决问题有实际用处
senses.definition: to provide information that can change what someone decides to do
senses.definitionCN: 指提供能改变某人行动决定的信息
senses.example: Any advice that can be relevant to the repair should be written down before the crew leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 任何可能对维修有用的建议，都应在工人离开前记下来。
senses.why: Usefulness is the practical face of relevance: the link must change an action, not just exist.
senses.whyCN: 有用性是相关性务实的一面：联系必须改变行动，而不只是存在。

senses.title: Legal relevance
senses.definition: to bear on a case in a way that a court is allowed to consider
senses.definitionCN: 指以法庭允许考虑的方式与案件相关
senses.example: The witness was asked whether the letter could be relevant to the dispute over the land.
senses.exampleCN: 证人被问到那封信是否可能与土地纠纷有关。
senses.why: Courts narrow the word further: many true facts are excluded because they do not bear on the charge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭把这个词收得更紧：很多真实事实因与指控无关而被排除。

senses.title: Statistical association
senses.definition: to be connected with another variable in a measurable way, without implying cause
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一个变量存在可测量的联系，但不含因果含义
senses.example: A variable that can be relevant to the outcome must be recorded from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 可能与结果有关的变量必须从第一天起就记录下来。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the word for measurable association and refuses to let it mean cause.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这个词留给可测量的关联，拒绝让它等同于因果。

senses.title: Relevance to a learner's life
senses.definition: to connect with what students already know or care about
senses.definitionCN: 指与学生已有的经验或关心的事建立联系
senses.example: A lesson that can be relevant to a student's own street will be remembered longer.
senses.exampleCN: 一堂能与学生自己那条街联系起来的课，会被记得更久。
senses.why: Teachers use the word for the bridge between a subject and a life, not for the subject alone.
senses.whyCN: 教师用这个词指学科与生活之间的桥，而不是学科本身。

senses.title: Timeliness
senses.definition: to matter at this particular moment rather than in general
senses.definitionCN: 指在此时此地的具体时刻有意义，而非泛泛地有意义
senses.example: An old rule can be relevant to a new dispute if the same conditions return.
senses.exampleCN: 如果相同条件重现，一条旧规则就可能与新的争端有关。
senses.why: Something can be true for centuries and relevant only today, which is why the word pairs with time.
senses.whyCN: 有的事真了几百年，却只今天才有意义，所以这个词常与时间连用。

senses.title: Weight in an argument
senses.definition: to affect how strongly a conclusion should be held
senses.definitionCN: 指影响一个结论应当被坚持到什么程度
senses.example: One more piece of evidence can be relevant to the final decision without settling it.
senses.exampleCN: 再多一份证据可能对最终决定有分量，却仍不能把它定下来。
senses.why: Bearing weight is the argumentative sense: the fact enters the scale even if it does not tip it.
senses.whyCN: 「有分量」是论证义：事实上了天平，哪怕没有压翻它。

senses.title: Staying on topic
senses.definition: to fit the point under discussion rather than wander from it
senses.definitionCN: 指贴合正在讨论的要点而不跑题
senses.example: A remark that can be relevant to the topic should come before personal stories.
senses.exampleCN: 与话题有关的发言应放在个人故事之前。
senses.why: In conversation the word becomes a rule of order: what is relevant is what keeps the thread.
senses.whyCN: 在日常对话里，这个词变成一条秩序规则：切题的就是接得住话头的。

intro.en: Relevant goes back to Latin relevare, to raise or lighten, from re- and levare, to lift, itself from levis, light in weight. Old French passed it to Scots law, where it meant pertinent to a case, and general English took it from there. The phrase be relevant to is a modern English frame whose first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: relevant 上溯拉丁语 relevare「抬起、减轻」，由 re- 与 levare「举起」构成，而 levare 又出自 levis「轻」。古法语把它传给苏格兰法律用语，意为「与案件有关」，一般英语再从那里借来。短语「be relevant to」是近代英语框架，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, the opposite of heavy, and it is the root of several lifting words.
items.cn: levis 意为重量轻的，与「重」相对，是好几个「举起」类词的根。

items.en: Re- plus levare produced relevare, to raise up or relieve, the source of both relieve and relevant.
items.cn: re- 与 levare 合成 relevare「抬起、减轻」，「缓解」与「相关」两词都出自它。

items.en: Old French used relevant in the legal sense of pertinent, and Scots law adopted it early.
items.cn: 古法语把 relevant 用于「切题、与案有关」的法律义，苏格兰法律很早就采用了。

items.en: English first used the word for evidence that bears on a case, a sense still central today.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指与案件有关的证据，这个义项至今仍是核心。

items.en: From the courtroom the word spread to ordinary argument, and the of or to frame is a later construction whose first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 从法庭扩散到日常论证后，接 of 或 to 的框架是更晚的构造，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks alike and shares the lifting root or the same stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of connection and fitness.
note.cn: 第一组形近，共享「抬起」词根或同一词干；第二组是与「关联、切合」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Connected through a relationship, from a different Latin verb meaning to carry back; it does not judge usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过关系相连，出自另一个意为「带回」的拉丁动词；它不评价是否有用。

entries.definition: To show or have a connection, again from the carrying-back verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示或存在联系，同样出自「带回」那个动词。

entries.definition: A connection or a family tie, not a judgement of pertinence.
entries.definitionCN: 指联系或亲属关系，不含「切题」的判断。

entries.definition: The quality of bearing on the matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议题有关的性质。

entries.definition: Having no bearing on the matter at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议题毫无关系。

entries.definition: Directly to the point, often sharper and more formal than relevant.
entries.definitionCN: 指直接切题，通常比本词更锐利、更正式。

entries.definition: Able to be applied to a particular case.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以适用于某一具体情况。

entries.definition: Closely connected and fitting, a formal word for relevance.
entries.definitionCN: 指密切相关且贴切，是「相关」的正式说法。

entries.definition: To have a connection with and affect a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某事有关并对其产生影响。

entries.definition: To be able to be used in a given situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指能在特定情境中使用。

entries.definition: To be linked in some way, without judging value.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某种方式相连，不评价价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations lift the word out of a pile, separate it from related, and borrow the courtroom where the word grew up.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把有用的东西从一堆里「抬」出来，把它与「有联系」分开，再借它长大的法庭场景记住。

normal.en: Levare is to lift, so relevant is what you lift out of a pile because it matters now.
normal.cn: levare 是「举起」，所以 relevant 就是从一堆材料里因为此刻要紧而被抬出来的那几份。

normal.en: Related only says two things are joined; relevant says the join changes your decision.
normal.cn: related 只说两件事连着，relevant 说这个连接会改变你的决定。

normal.en: The word grew up in court, where only facts that bear on the charge are allowed in.
normal.cn: 这个词长在法庭里，只有与指控有关的事实才被允许进入。

normal.en: Remember the two prepositions: relevant to a question, relevant for a purpose.
normal.cn: 记住两个介词：与问题相关用 to，对某目的有用也可用 for。

normal.en: Irrelevant is the direct negation and needs no extra words.
normal.cn: irrelevant 是直接否定，不必再加别的词。

abstract.en: Relevance is a spotlight, not a lamp: it lights one spot and leaves the rest in shadow.
abstract.cn: 相关性像聚光灯而非照明灯：它照亮一处，其余留在阴影里。

abstract.en: A fact can be true forever and relevant only for one afternoon.
abstract.cn: 一个事实可以永远为真，却只在一个下午有意义。

abstract.en: To call something irrelevant is often a quiet way of refusing to argue with it.
abstract.cn: 说某事不相关，常常是拒绝与之争论的一种温和方式。

examples.en: The report should include only data that can be relevant to the research question.
examples.cn: 报告只应收入可能与研究问题有关的数据。

examples.en: His experience in the mountains can be relevant to the rescue plan for the valley.
examples.cn: 他在山区的经验可能对山谷的救援方案有用。

examples.en: A question about cost can be relevant to the choice of material.
examples.cn: 关于成本的问题可能对材料的选择有影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 瑞勒文特 图」——从一叠里抬出有用的那份：与……相关

root: 拉丁语 relevare「抬起、减轻」（re-「再」+ levare「举起」，源于 levis「轻」），经法语进入英语，先作法律术语「与案件有关」；短语框架属近代英语，首见年代不确定。形近的 related 出自 referre 的过去分词 relatus，词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all test a connection against a purpose: the matter at hand, a problem, a court case, a variable, a learner's life, the present moment, an argument and the thread of talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在用「目的」检验联系：眼前议题、待解问题、案件、变量、学习者生活、当下时刻、论证分量与谈话线索。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: only the few sheets that bear on the case are pushed into the middle of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：只有与案子有关的那几页被推到桌子中间。

branches.en: THE LIFT: what matters now is lifted out of the pile.
branches.cn: 抬起：此刻要紧的东西从一堆里被抬出来。

branches.en: THE USE: the lifted sheet must change what someone does.
branches.cn: 用处：抬出来的那页必须能改变某人的行动。

branches.en: THE COURT AND THE TABLE: a charge limits what counts, and a variable limits what can be measured.
branches.cn: 法庭与表格：指控限定什么算数，变量限定什么可测。

branches.en: THE LEARNER AND THE HOUR: a lesson must reach a life, and a rule must reach this moment.
branches.cn: 学习者与此刻：课要够得着生活，规则要够得着当下。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT AND THE THREAD: a fact can tilt a decision, and a remark must keep the talk going.
branches.cn: 分量与话头：事实能压动决定，发言要接得住话头。

intro.en: The family is built from a Latin verb of lifting, with negation and endings marking the grammatical roles.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁语「举起」动词构成，否定前缀与词尾负责标出语法角色。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare, relevare and levis supply the core; in- and -ance, -ant, -ly build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare、relevare 与 levis 提供核心，in- 与 -ance、-ant、-ly 构成其余部分。

senses.title: Rock fragments
senses.definition: in geology, loose broken rock material produced by weathering
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中由风化作用产生的松散岩石碎块
senses.example: Detritus from the cliff feeds the beach below.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖上落下的岩屑为下方的海滩提供沉积物。
senses.why: Geology uses the oldest technical sense: material worn or rubbed off a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 地质学使用的是最古老的技术义项：从更大物体上被磨损、摩擦下来的材料。

senses.title: Dead organic fragments
senses.definition: in ecology, the dead plant and animal fragments that accumulate in soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中积聚在土壤或水体中的死亡动植物碎片
senses.example: Detritus on the river bed supports a dense community of invertebrates.
senses.exampleCN: 河床上的腐屑支撑着密集的无脊椎动物群落。
senses.why: The geological image transfers to organic remains: what is broken off is now dead tissue rather than rock.
senses.whyCN: 地质形象移用到有机物上：被拆散下来的不再是岩石，而是死亡组织。

senses.title: Rubble and wreckage
senses.definition: loose debris left by construction, demolition or war
senses.definitionCN: 施工、拆除或战争留下的松散废弃物
senses.example: Detritus from the collapsed wall blocked the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 倒塌墙体留下的瓦砾堵住了小巷。
senses.why: Human demolition produces the same kind of loose fragments, so the word moves easily from cliffs to cities.
senses.whyCN: 人类拆建会产生同样的松散碎块，因此这个词从悬崖轻易移到了城市。

senses.title: Remains of a body
senses.definition: in forensic or archaeological contexts, the scattered remains of a decomposed body
senses.definitionCN: 法医或考古语境中分解尸体散落的残骸
senses.example: Investigators recovered bone detritus from the shallow grave.
senses.exampleCN: 调查人员从浅坑中取回了骨骼残骸。
senses.why: A body that has broken down leaves fragments, and the neutral noun avoids the emotional weight of corpse.
senses.whyCN: 分解后的尸体会留下碎片，这个中性名词避开了 corpse 的情绪重量。

senses.title: Sinking particles
senses.definition: in oceanography, organic particles sinking from surface waters, often called marine snow
senses.definitionCN: 海洋学中从表层水域下沉的有机颗粒，常称「海洋雪」
senses.example: Deep-sea detritus supplies food to communities far below the sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 深海碎屑为远离阳光的群落提供食物。
senses.why: Open-ocean ecology extends the term to particles in transit, because they are fragments of dead matter falling through water.
senses.whyCN: 开阔海洋生态学把这个词扩展到沉降中的颗粒，因为它们也是穿过水体下沉的死亡物质碎片。

senses.title: Soil's mineral crumbs
senses.definition: in soil science, the mineral grains and rock fragments that form part of the parent material
senses.definitionCN: 土壤学中构成母质一部分的矿物颗粒与岩石碎片
senses.example: The soil's detritus comes mostly from weathered granite.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土壤的矿物碎屑主要来自风化的花岗岩。
senses.why: Soil science keeps the geological sense alive inside the profile, where fragments are not yet soil.
senses.whyCN: 土壤学在剖面中保留了地质义项，那里的碎块尚未变成土壤。

senses.title: Leftovers of an idea or culture
senses.definition: figuratively, the small remnants of a system, tradition or idea that survive after its decline
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指体系、传统或观念衰落后仍存留的细小残余
senses.example: The essay traces the detritus of an older philosophy in modern policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在现代政策中追寻一种旧哲学的残余。
senses.why: The metaphor follows the literal sense: what remains of a larger thing is small, scattered and no longer whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻沿用了字面义：更大事物留下的东西是细小的、散落的、不再完整。

senses.title: Stone chips in an excavation
senses.definition: in archaeology, the small stone chips and flakes left by tool-making or building
senses.definitionCN: 考古学中制作工具或营建活动留下的碎石片
senses.example: The floor layer held detritus from flint knapping.
senses.exampleCN: 地面层中留有打制燧石产生的石屑。
senses.why: Archaeology reads behaviour from the small fragments left behind, so the word names evidence rather than waste.
senses.whyCN: 考古学从留下的小碎片读出行为，因此这个词指证据，而不是垃圾。

intro.en: Detritus is a Latin past participle used as a noun: 'that which has been rubbed away'.
intro.cn: detritus 是一个作名词用的拉丁语过去分词，意为「被磨掉的东西」。

items.en: Latin deterere means 'to rub away, wear down'. It joins de- 'away' and terere 'to rub', the same verb behind trite and attrition.
items.cn: 拉丁语 deterere 意为「磨掉、磨蚀」，由 de-「离开」与 terere「摩擦」构成；trite 与 attrition 也出自同一个动词。

items.en: The neuter past participle detritum, used as a noun, is Latin detritus. English borrowed the form directly, keeping its Latin look.
items.cn: 中性过去分词 detritum 用作名词即拉丁语 detritus。英语直接借用了这一形式，保留了它的拉丁语外观。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology adopted detritus for loose weathered rock, when sedimentary processes were being described systematically. The precise first use is not certain.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学在系统描述沉积过程时，采用 detritus 指松散的风化岩石。确切首见出处并不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology extended the word to organic fragments in soil, rivers and the sea, giving rise to the detritus food chain.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把这个词扩展到土壤、河流与海洋中的有机碎片，并由此产生「碎屑食物链」的说法。

items.en: Forensic and archaeological writing later used detritus for scattered remains and tool-making chips, where fragments are read as evidence.
items.cn: 法医与考古写作随后用 detritus 指散落的残骸与制石碎片，此时碎片被当作证据来解读。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root or looks close; the second holds near-synonyms for fragments.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根或形近；第二组是表示碎片的近义词。

entries.definition: Describing material made of detritus, as in detrital rock; the noun names the material itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由碎屑构成的材料，如碎屑岩；名词本身指材料。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on detritus; it is the consumer, not the fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 以碎屑为食的动物；它是取食者，不是碎屑本身。

entries.definition: Harm or damage, from Latin detrimentum, 'a wearing away'; it shares deterere with detritus but long ago left the physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 损害、伤害，来自拉丁语 detrimentum「磨损」；与 detritus 共享 deterere，但早已离开物理义。

entries.definition: Scattered fragments of destroyed material, borrowed from French; detritus is more technical and includes organic fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 被毁材料散落的碎片，借自法语；detritus 更技术化，且包含有机碎片。

entries.definition: Material that has settled to the bottom of water or been laid down; detritus may be suspended before it becomes sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 沉降到水底或被铺设下来的材料；detritus 在成为沉积物之前可能仍悬浮。

entries.definition: Large irregular pieces of broken stone or brick; detritus usually means finer fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 破碎石头或砖块的大而不规则的块体；detritus 通常指更细的碎片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin rubbing image and the scientific collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语「摩擦」意象与科学搭配。

normal.en: Latin deterere 'rub away' gives detritus, detrition and detriment.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 deterere「磨掉」产生 detritus、detrition、detriment。

normal.en: The collocations mark the fields: organic detritus, leaf detritus, detritus food chain.
normal.cn: 搭配标出领域：有机碎屑、叶片碎屑、碎屑食物链。

normal.en: The adjective is detrital, the eater is a detritivore.
normal.cn: 形容词是 detrital，取食者是 detritivore。

normal.en: Detritus is uncountable: you speak of a layer of detritus, not of detrituses.
normal.cn: detritus 不可数：说 a layer of detritus，而不说 detrituses。

normal.en: The river bend with its mat of leaves is the word's clearest scene.
normal.cn: 河湾里那层叶片垫，是这个词最清楚的场景。

abstract.en: Think of a cliff's slow donation to the beach: every grain was once part of something larger.
abstract.cn: 想象悬崖缓慢地馈赠海滩：每一粒都曾是更大事物的一部分。

abstract.en: A culture's detritus is what survives when the building is gone: habits, phrases, small rituals.
abstract.cn: 一种文化的残余是建筑消失后仍留下的东西：习惯、说法、小小的仪式。

abstract.en: Marine snow is detritus falling like slow weather through dark water.
abstract.cn: 海洋雪就是碎屑像缓慢的天气一样落过黑暗水体。

examples.en: Organic detritus in the soil feeds the decomposers below it.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机碎屑供养其下方的分解者。

examples.en: The flood left a layer of detritus across the field.
examples.cn: 洪水在田野上留下一层碎屑。

examples.en: Archaeologists sifted the detritus for clues about tool-making.
examples.cn: 考古学家筛检这些碎屑，寻找关于制石工具的线索。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（掉）+ tri（碎）+ tus → 掉下来的碎东西 → 碎屑、腐屑

root: 拉丁语 detritus，为 deterere「磨掉、磨蚀」的过去分词（de-「离开」+ terere「摩擦」）→ 字面「被磨掉的东西」→ 碎屑、腐屑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe fragments separated from something larger: rock, dead tissue, buildings, bodies, sinking particles, soil grains, ideas and stone chips.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述从更大事物上分离出来的碎片：岩石、死亡组织、建筑、尸体、沉降颗粒、土壤颗粒、观念与石屑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small pieces that were once part of a larger whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：曾是更大整体一部分的小碎片。

branches.en: THE MINERAL: weathering breaks rock into fragments that later become sediment or soil parent material.
branches.cn: 矿物：风化把岩石打碎成碎片，这些碎片后来成为沉积物或土壤母质。

branches.en: THE ORGANIC: dead tissue becomes detritus on land, in rivers and in the deep sea.
branches.cn: 有机：死亡组织在陆地、河流与深海中都成为碎屑。

branches.en: THE RUIN: demolition and war leave the same kind of loose fragments at human scale.
branches.cn: 废墟：拆建与战争在人类尺度上留下同类松散碎片。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: scattered body remains and knapping chips are read as traces of past events.
branches.cn: 证据：散落的遗体残骸与打石碎片被读作往昔事件的痕迹。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: ideas also leave small remains after the larger system declines.
branches.cn: 隐喻：更大的体系衰落后，观念同样会留下细小残余。

intro.en: Detritus is a Latin participle form, not an English compound.
intro.cn: detritus 是拉丁语分词形式，不是英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin terere 'to rub', behind detritus, detrition, trite and attrition, with the prefix de- 'away'.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 terere「摩擦」，detritus、detrition、trite、attrition 都出自它，并带前缀 de-「离开」。

items.example: Detritus carpets the slow part of the stream.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑铺满溪流流速较缓的地段。

items.meaning: made of or relating to detritus
items.meaningCN: 由碎屑构成或与碎屑有关的
items.example: Detrital rock forms from compressed fragments.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑岩由压实的碎片形成。

items.example: The detritivore feeds on the leaf mat.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑动物取食叶片垫。
食碎屑鱼类在底部觅食。

items.example: Detrition shapes the pebbles over centuries.
items.exampleCN: 磨蚀在数百年间塑造了这些卵石。

items.meaningCN: 因过度使用而磨损，故指陈腐的
items.example: Trite and detritus share the idea of rubbing.
items.exampleCN: trite 与 detritus 共享「摩擦」这一概念。

items.example: Attrition reduces the fragments to sand.
items.exampleCN: 磨耗把这些碎片变成沙子。

items.example: Debris is not related to detritus by root.
items.exampleCN: debris 与 detritus 在词根上并无亲缘关系。
